title: Arsenal 2 – Chelsea 1: better team won
description: That was about as one-sided of a 2-1 match as you’ll ever see. Arsenal thoroughly outplayed Chelsea, shutting down their free-scoring attack, and playing dazzling attacking football of their own (at times). You’d really prefer it if the Gunners would put a couple more in the back of the net so we aren’t left sweating […]
fullText:
That was about as one-sided of a 2-1 match as you'll ever see. Arsenal thoroughly outplayed Chelsea, shutting down their free-scoring attack, and playing dazzling attacking football of their own (at times). You'd really prefer it if the Gunners would put a couple 

Arsenal went behind inside two minutes. At the risk of sounding overly dismissive and minimizing a good strike from Morgan Rogers, it was a pretty lucky goal for Chelsea. It started from a free kick awarded for a soft foul. The ball bounced around from one side to another in / around the box. A "keep the ball alive header" fell quite kindly for Rogers. And he took it as well as a player possibly could at a screened David Raya who was leaning the opposite direction to see around the traffic. Of course it had to be Morgan Rogers, too. Sometimes it be like that.

The Gunners responded really well, though. They immediately took control of the match and had the ball in the back of the net within 10-15 minutes of conceding. Riccardo Calafiori's would-be equalizer was correctly ruled out for an offside by Ezri Konsa, but Arsenal kept pressing.

They were rewarded in the 25th minute when Kai Havertz found the back of the net, as he often does against his former club. Find you someone who loves you as much as Kai Havertz loves scoring against Chelsea. The German winger was given far too much time and space to drive inside from the right wing. He saw Emi Martinez leaning / cheating to the far post and beat the Argentine keeper with a low shot to the near post. And speaking of things players often do against their former clubs, Emi Martinez got fingertips on the shot but couldn't keep it out. I will never tire of watching him concede "should have done better" goals against Arsenal.

Chelsea nearly smashed-and-grabbed a halftime lead just before the whistle, but Pedro Neto's shot hit the post. It probably served as a good reminder for the Arsenal defense of the threat that Chelsea could carry on the break, even if those counterattacking opportunities were mostly well-controlled by Arsenal's midfield and ball-possession.

Sidenote: it annoys me when announcers don't acknowledge that goalkeepers set themselves up to defend the goal and don't care about shots onto the post. If a shot goes onto the post (and out), it hasn't gone into the net, and that's kind of the entire point of goalkeeping. I'd suggest that is precisely what David Raya did on the Pedro Neto chance at the end of the first half. I also think Gabriel's pressure, even though he didn't get the block, was important because it kept Neto from fully following through to shape his shot.

Arsenal scored a brilliant goal early in the second half that would prove enough to claim the points. Christos Tzolis, who had a much better game than last week against Aston Villa, played an excellent ball across the middle. Kai Havertz dummied it through, freezing the defenders, which helped make Martin Ødegaard even more wide open in the middle. (Can you be more wide open or are you just wide open?) The Arsenal skipper buried it, lifting it over and around a helpless Martinez.

The amount of time and space Martin Ødegaard had in the middle of the Chelsea box, virtually unmarked by any defender typifies the current state of the Blues. They're a collection of players, with plenty of excellent attacking pieces mind you, but they aren't a team. They don't press in tandem. They don't defend as a unit. Guys are running around trying to make plays, and in doing so, opening up all sorts of spaces in the formation.

Xabi Alonso has his work cut out for him. He's a quality coach and probably can do it, in a vacuum. Whether he'll be given enough time to straighten things out at a club that isn't known for having patience with managers is an open question. And the individual vs. collective thing on display today gives me pause, too. Does Xabi Alonso have the secret sauce to get a reportedly headstrong group of players to row together when several other mangers couldn't? The fact that he lost the power struggle against his players at Real Madrid doesn't bode particularly well for him!

Back to today's match. Arsenal generated more than 2.0 xG (2.1-2.35 is what I've seen) and held Chelsea to 0.35 xG. Coming into today's match, the Blues had 5.97 xG from two matches played. The shot chart from today is textbook, from an Arsenal perspective. The Gunners took their shots from dangerous, central areas and limited the Blues to attempts from wide and distance.

Arsenal's first three matches account for the first, third, and fourth lowest xGA so far this Premier League season. Our defense is really, really good. And we're doing it without two first choice players in William Saliba and Jurrien Timber.

Martin Ødegaard was excellent. It's night and day with him, which is apropos because most people think some of his struggles last season were due to having a newborn around that was keeping him from sleeping. Mikel Arteta mentioned that the skipper's "personal life" settling down was helpful. The combination of Ødegaard and Havertz, with Tzolis adding technical quality and chance creation from the left wing, makes the attack so much better. The difference between Havertz / MØ and Gyokeres / Merino to close out the match was stark, and not in a good way. Bruno Guimaraes, who was an unused substitute, should help with the substitution / rotation, but Mikel Arteta needs to be acutely aware of maintaining the on-ball technical level throughout the match.

Gabriel played up to his O Monstro nickname. He was excellent. There was nothing in his accidental kick to Emi Martinez's head early in the match. Both players were on the ground, scrambling for the ball in the goal mouth. That sort of thing happens. If the referee had really wanted to be harsh (silly), he could have shown a yellow.

Cole Palmer, on the other hand, was lucky to stay on the pitch. Lee Dixon thought he "100%" should have been booked for whacking Myles Lewis-Skelly's legs out from under him midway through the first half. He then was properly booked for pulling Kai Havertz down from behind to prevent a promising attack. He then kicked the ball away before the ensuing restart, something the referee booked Joao Pedro for doing earlier in the half.

I am eagerly (not) looking forward to all the times this season that opposing players aren't booked for waving an imaginary card at the referee now that we've had an Arsenal player (Tzolis) booked for it.

Ezri Konsa had a mixed game in his first start. He turned his back on the play on Chelsea's goal and badly misjudged a bouncing ball later in the first half. He also had a tremendous sliding tackle to bail out a bad Riccardo Calafiori giveaway and punish a loose touch from Morgan Rogers.

Calafiori will continue to be an X-factor and difference-maker as long as he can stay fit and available. Piero Hincapie bringing tons of energy as a substitute should help. That becoming a regular pattern will be great for all involved.

Morgan Rogers will fit right in at Chelsea. His frustration and temper was on full display late in the game when he got himself booked for yelling, remonstrating at, and shoving Declan Rice. To be fair, Rice did catch him running up the pitch — he clipped his heels cutting behind him. Whether / how much the Arsenal man knew about it is up to you. Clearly, Rogers felt a certain way about it.

Bukayo Saka continues to run cold against Chelsea. He had two pretty good chances turned away — one a save Martinez should make and one a strong stop.

Arsenal have scored six goals this season, all from open play. It took the club 10 PL matches to reach that mark last season.

With the caveat that Arsenal are a really, really good team that does this to plenty of opponents, I'm coming away from today's match much less impressed by / worried about Chelsea. They've got a lot of work to do. Maybe they'll put it together. They have enough talent to be towards the top of the table and they'll be greatly helped by playing one match per week.

We're excellent, folks. Three wins from three and we look better than we did down the stretch. It's all about being able to maintain that level for longer than they did last season. You'd have made a lot of money betting on Hull City to be the last team to concede a Premier League goal this season.

title: Brighton 0-1 Arsenal: Baum shines on debut
description: Lisa Baum marked her Arsenal debut in spectacular fashion as her first-half strike secured a 0-1 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion in the Gunners’ opening Barclays Women’s Super League fixture o...
fullText:
Lisa Baum marked her Arsenal debut in spectacular fashion as her first-half strike secured a 0-1 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion in the Gunners' opening Barclays Women's Super League fixture of the season.

The 19-year-old summer arrival from RB Leipzig produced the decisive moment after only 10 minutes at Broadfield Stadium, driving through the Brighton defense before firing an unstoppable effort off the underside of the crossbar.

It was not always comfortable for Renée Slegers' side, who had opportunities to extend their advantage but were also forced to withstand periods of Brighton pressure. Ultimately, though, Arsenal did enough to leave Sussex with three points from a ground where they had failed to win on their previous two WSL visits.

Slegers named four summer signings in her starting XI, with Baum joined by Misa Rodríguez, Ona Batlle and Georgia Stanway. And it was Rodríguez who was required to make the first significant intervention of the afternoon.

Brighton goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie launched a precise ball over Arsenal's defensive line inside the opening five minutes, releasing Kiko Seike into space. The Japan international managed to escape Batlle and get her shot away, but Rodríguez reacted well to make a low save.

Five minutes later, another Arsenal debutant made an even greater impact.

Baum regained possession inside Brighton territory before driving directly at the home defense. She carried the ball into the penalty area and, rather than looking for a teammate, unleashed a fierce strike towards the near post. Nnadozie had little chance as the ball crashed against the underside of the crossbar and crossed the line.

Ten minutes into her Arsenal career, Baum had her first WSL goal.

While Arsenal's new arrivals were experiencing their first taste of WSL football in red and white, there was also a particularly familiar figure lining up on the opposite side.

Lia Wälti made her Brighton debut against the club where she spent seven years and established herself as one of the most respected figures of Arsenal's modern era.

The Swiss midfielder had returned to England this summer following one season with Juventus, but her first competitive assignment in Brighton colours immediately brought her face-to-face with her former club.

Wälti's connection with Arsenal extends far beyond simply being a former player. Across seven seasons with the Gunners, she became an integral part of the midfield and a hugely popular figure among supporters and teammates alike, leaving behind the status of a genuine club legend when her time in north London came to an end.

Her presence gave the opening-day encounter an additional layer of significance.

Now tasked with helping Brighton compete against the side she represented for so long, Wälti brought experience and composure to Arturo Ruiz's midfield as the Seagulls attempted to recover from Baum's early breakthrough.

Arsenal should have doubled their lead almost immediately.

Olivia Smith's pressure forced Manuela Vanegas into surrendering possession before the Canadian found Alessia Russo in space inside the penalty area. With the goal at her mercy, however, Russo sent her effort over the crossbar.

The England striker was presented with another opportunity later in the half when she broke through one-on-one, but Nnadozie quickly closed down the space and made the save.

Mariona Caldentey also tested the Brighton goalkeeper from the edge of the area as Arsenal searched for the comfort of a second.

Brighton remained a threat themselves, particularly through Seike. The winger's pace provided Arsenal with a consistent problem on the transition, although Batlle recovered well after being caught out by the early opportunity.

Fran Kirby had one of Brighton's better chances shortly before the interval. Vanegas knocked a long delivery into her path inside the area, but the former Chelsea forward sent her first-time attempt over Rodríguez's goal.

Arsenal therefore went into the break ahead, although their failure to capitalise on several promising openings ensured Brighton remained firmly in the contest.

Ruiz's side emerged for the second half with renewed intent.

Marisa Olislagers was involved in an early opportunity for the hosts, but Rodríguez dealt with the danger as Brighton attempted to force Arsenal onto the back foot.

The visitors gradually regained control of possession, and Baum continued to demonstrate why she had been handed an immediate starting role.

The German youngster worked her way into the penalty area and delivered a dangerous low ball across goal, which Brighton eventually scrambled clear. She later drove forward once again before shooting directly at Nnadozie.

Kim Little also tested the Brighton goalkeeper as Arsenal continued searching for a second goal that would ease the tension.

But Brighton refused to disappear from the contest.

Seike remained their most dangerous attacking outlet and came particularly close when her effort took a deflection off Batlle before travelling narrowly wide.

With Arsenal still protecting only a one-goal advantage, the closing stages became increasingly open.

Baum's impressive debut eventually came to an end when she was replaced by Caitlin Foord, who quickly became involved by sending an attempt over the crossbar.

Brighton continued searching for an equaliser and Charlie Rule threatened from the edge of the penalty area, but her first-time effort cleared the bar.

At the opposite end, Arsenal had another opportunity to finally put the contest beyond the hosts.

Russo released substitute Stina Blackstenius, whose low effort looked destined for the bottom corner until Nnadozie produced another excellent save.

That meant Arsenal had to negotiate six minutes of additional time with their slender advantage intact.

Rather than retreating completely, Slegers' side looked to control possession and limit Brighton's opportunities to launch one final attack. They succeeded, seeing out the remaining minutes to secure their first three points of the new campaign.

It was far from a flawless Arsenal performance. The Gunners created enough opportunities to make the afternoon considerably more comfortable and will know they need to be more clinical as the season develops. Brighton, meanwhile, provided enough threat to ensure the result remained uncertain until the final whistle.

But after failing to win on their previous two league visits to Broadfield Stadium, the result was significant.

With London rivals Chelsea dropping points against Aston Villa in their own opening fixture, Arsenal have immediately put three points on the board as they attempt to challenge for a first WSL title in seven years.

And while there will be plenty for Slegers to analyse, the defining image from Arsenal's opening afternoon belonged to one of her newest players.

Ten minutes into her competitive debut, Baum announced herself to English football in emphatic fashion, and ultimately delivered the moment Arsenal needed to begin their campaign with a victory.

title: 5 NFL Teams That Will Let Fan Bases Down in Week 1
description: Every team has a clean slate right now, but of course, not all 32 NFL teams can start their season […]
fullText:
Every team has a clean slate right now, but of course, not all 32 NFL teams can start their season with a 1-0 record. While a Week 1 loss doesn't mean anything in the grand scheme of things, it's not how any team wants to begin the season. Yet, here are five NFL teams who will inevitably let their fan bases down in Week 1.

Whenever a team wins a Super Bowl, changes and new challenges follow into the next year. In this case, the Seattle Seahawks have lost their offensive playcaller, the Super Bowl LX MVP, and a Pro Bowl cornerback. While the front office is one of the best in business, including head coach Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks are also taking on a worthy opponent in the New England Patriots, who will be out for revenge. In other words, don't be surprised if the Seahawks start their season with a losing record.

Realizing last year's performance was nowhere near good enough, the Tennessee Titans cleaned house and surprisingly decided to move forward with a defensive-minded head coach. But what about Cam Ward's development? The No. 1 pick from 2025 finished with the third-lowest completion rate last season. While Ward may very well be poised to make a sizable second-year leap, these things tend to take time, building up over the course of a season. Ward may be improved, but it may take him some time to find his confidence, and the New York Jets are also playing with their backs against the wall as coach Aaron Glenn kicks off the year on the hot seat.

While the Green Bay Packers could prove to be Super Bowl contenders by the end of the season, the start of the year could get a bit rocky. Playing without two key starters, Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons, the Packers will be relying on unproven players to fill sizable roles. Not to mention, they're facing off against a good and familiar opponent on the road against the Minnesota Vikings. Despite high expectations, the Packers' road could be bumpy to begin with.

John Harbaugh may be able to whip this New York Giants team into a playoff contender over the course of the season. Unfortunately, they get a pretty tough test in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Jaxson Dart is still unproven as a quarterback, and Malik Nabers likely won't be at 100% (if he's available at all), which will only place more stress on their second-year QB. Meanwhile, the Cowboys have one of the NFL's best offenses and a remade defense that has potential. The Giants should be able to keep this one competitive, but a Week 1 loss is not how any fan base wants to start the season.

The Kansas City Chiefs are flying a bit under the radar as the regular season approaches. That's likely exactly how Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, and Co. want it after missing out on the postseason in 2025. Yet, we know this team has potential, and they're extremely well-coached. Of course, so are the Denver Broncos. But the Chiefs not only have something to prove, they'll be working with home-field advantage too. It may be one of the few losses suffered by the Broncos all season, but a Week 1 wake-up call may be just what they need to kick off a Super Bowl campaign.

title: Former Real Madrid striker has 6G/A but just one start in La Liga this season
description: The remarkable opening to the new campaign being enjoyed by Deportivo Alavés star Mariano Díaz continued on Sunday. This came courtesy of his exploits in a La Liga meeting with Osasuna.Alavés, as ...
fullText:
The remarkable opening to the new campaign being enjoyed by Deportivo Alavés star Mariano Díaz continued on Sunday. This came courtesy of his exploits in a La Liga meeting with Osasuna.

Alavés, as a collective, are fresh off keeping alive what has been a stellar start to the season on the domestic front.

After welcoming Osasuna to Vitoria-Gasteiz this evening, Quique Sánchez Flores' troops ultimately emerged on the right side of a 5-2 result. This made it 10 points from an available 12 in 2026/27, good enough for a place in 2nd in the La Liga table.

And the aforementioned Mariano Díaz, again, was right at the heart of things…

Not long removed from spending a full year away from professional football, ex-Real Madrid hitman Mariano was afforded his first start of the term on Sunday.

And the 33-year-old responded with a starring performance, laying on the assist for the game's opener before turning goalscorer himself not long after.

All told, remarkably, this means that Mariano has now racked up six direct goal contributions (3G,3A) in just four appearances (1 start!) in La Liga this season.

title: Former Liverpool star set to complete transfer move amid Chelsea links
description: Liverpool Favourite Gini Wijnaldum Set for New Move After Chelsea InterestFormer Liverpool midfielder Gini Wijnaldum appears to have settled his future, with the 35-year-old reportedly undergoing a me...
fullText:
Former Liverpool midfielder Gini Wijnaldum appears to have settled his future, with the 35-year-old reportedly undergoing a medical ahead of a move to Al-Ittihad.

Wijnaldum became a free agent following his departure from Al-Ettifaq and briefly found himself linked with Chelsea. A return to the Premier League would certainly have added another intriguing chapter to a career already packed with major moments.

Instead, the Netherlands international looks set to remain in Saudi Arabia.

According to Ben Jacobs, Wijnaldum is set to sign for Al-Ittihad on a 1+1 contract, with a medical currently taking place.

There is some logic to the decision. Wijnaldum already knows the Saudi Pro League extremely well after joining Al-Ettifaq from Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, and his performances last season suggested there remains plenty left in the tank.

The midfielder scored 16 goals and registered six assists during the 2025/26 Saudi Pro League campaign. Those are substantial numbers for a player who has built much of his reputation around tactical intelligence, positioning and midfield discipline.

At 35, Wijnaldum has seemingly found an environment where he can continue playing regularly while maintaining an impressive level of productivity.

Chelsea had reportedly explored the possibility of bringing Wijnaldum back to England as they considered their midfield options.

Such a transfer would have been fascinating from a Liverpool perspective. Wijnaldum spent five years at Anfield and became one of the most dependable components of Jürgen Klopp's great Liverpool side.

Ultimately, Chelsea's interest failed to develop into an agreement, with reports indicating that the London club were unlikely to pursue a deal.

That leaves Al-Ittihad positioned to secure an experienced midfielder who knows precisely what is required at the highest level.

For Liverpool supporters, Wijnaldum will always be associated with one extraordinary night at Anfield.

Signed from Newcastle United in 2016, he made 237 appearances for Liverpool and scored 22 goals. His contribution went considerably deeper than the raw numbers.

Wijnaldum played a crucial role as Liverpool won the Champions League in 2019 before ending their 30-year wait for a league championship by winning the Premier League in 2019/20.

His defining performance arrived against Barcelona in the 2019 Champions League semi-final.

Introduced at half-time, Wijnaldum scored twice in two minutes as Liverpool produced one of the most remarkable European comebacks Anfield has witnessed. Those goals ensured his place in Liverpool folklore.

He was equally valuable across the relentless demands of a league campaign, featuring in all 38 Premier League matches during Liverpool's title-winning season.

Wijnaldum eventually left Liverpool for PSG in 2021, bringing an understated but hugely significant Anfield career to an end.

Five years later, his journey continues.

Chelsea provided the possibility of an unexpected Premier League return, but Al-Ittihad now appear to have won the race for his signature.

Should the medical proceed as expected, Wijnaldum will begin another Saudi Pro League chapter with an impressive 2025/26 campaign behind him and a Liverpool legacy that remains secure.

title: Juventus fans pay tribute to Baresi ahead of Milan match: ‘With infinite respect’
description: Juventus fans paid tribute to Milan legend Franco Baresi ahead of this evening’s Serie A match, referencing a specific incident that left its mark in 1990.The game kicked off at the Allianz Juventus...
fullText:
Juventus fans paid tribute to Milan legend Franco Baresi ahead of this evening's Serie A match, referencing a specific incident that left its mark in 1990.

The game kicked off at the Allianz Juventus Stadium at 19.45 UK time (20.45 CEST).

You can follow all the action as it happens on the Liveblog.

There were emotional moments before kick-off, as it was the first meeting of the sides since the death of legendary Milan captain Baresi in July at the age of 66.

MILAN, ITALY – AUGUST 04: Franco Baresi's coffin arrives at the Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio during the funeral ceremony at Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio on August 04, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

There was a message on the big screens of the stadium in Turin that prompted a standing ovation from everyone in the arena.

"Class, style, leadership and respect, an example for generations of players and fans. His memory will live forever, with infinite respect, the applause of the Stadium is all for you."

MILAN, ITALY – DECEMBER 15: Franco Baresi looks on during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Genoa at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on December 15, 2024 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

The Juventus supporters also had their own more pointed tribute to Baresi, with a banner referencing a very specific moment in their shared history.

"07-03-1990: Thank you Baresi" read the banner.

It was a reference to the moment when Milan played at the Heysel Stadium in Brussels against Mechelen, the first time an Italian side had been there since the tragedy that saw 39 Juventus fans killed by the collapse of a wall.

Baresi and Milan had been told by the authorities they could not pay tribute before kick-off, but the captain took the 39 red roses anyway and walked over to the spot to lay them down, daring anyone to try and stop him.

title: Inside Harrison Smith's eleventh-hour deal to return to the Vikings
description: Vikings legend Harrison Smith is back for a fifteenth season in Minnesota.
fullText:
Vikings legend Harrison Smith is back for a fifteenth season in Minnesota. The initial reports regarding the contract ($12.25 million base, up to $16.25 million max) were surprising to some.

An executive from another team was skeptical of the reported value, based on Smith's performance in 2025 and the fact that he had been available to anyone, with no takers, throughout the offseason, training camp, and preseason.

The contract indeed carries a $12.25 million base package, technically. Here's the breakdown:

1. Signing bonus: $6.95 million.

2. 2026 base salary: $1.3 million.

3. 2026 per-game active roster bonus: $235,294 per game ($4 million total).

The $4 million in incentives are based on $1 million for earning a playoff berth (wild-card or bye), $1.5 million for winning in the divisional round, $2 million for winning the NFC Championship, or $4 million for winning the Super Bowl.

Basically, if the Vikings end up paying Smith $16.25 million, it will be the best money the franchise has ever spent.

The very high per-game roster bonuses reduce Smith's guarantee to $8.25 million. If he plays all year, he gets to $12.25 million.

Smith arguably has greater value to the Vikings than he would have to a new team. As one source put it, Smith is a "glue guy," whose mere presence makes the Minnesota defense and the rest of the team better.

As to his late availability, we're told that when other teams inquired about him, Smith made it clear that he wasn't going to attend training camp. Which made a return to Minnesota even more likely, if he decided to play for another season.

It may have been inevitable. Either way, Smith returns for one more run with the team that made him a first-round pick in 2012.

The defense is more than good enough to compete, and to contend. If the offense carries its weight, they could make the playoffs and win their first postseason game since 2019.

title: Clemson Tigers: Dabo Swinney Unsure About Starting QB After Week 1 Loss
description: The Clemson Tigers had a handful of question marks heading into the 2026 season, but none was as glaring as the quarterback position. After seeing Cade Klubnik enter the 2026 NFL Draft, coach Dabo Swinney elected not to get a quarterback out of the NCAA Transfer Portal and instead kept his options in-house. Christopher Vizzina […] The post Clemson Tigers: Dabo Swinney Unsure About Starting QB After Week 1 Loss appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Clemson Tigers had a handful of question marks heading into the 2026 season, but none was as glaring as the quarterback position. After seeing Cade Klubnik enter the 2026 NFL Draft, coach Dabo Swinney elected not to get a quarterback out of the NCAA Transfer Portal and instead kept his options in-house.

Christopher Vizzina was last season's backup quarterback, and incoming freshman Tait Reynolds was the other player vying for the starting quarterback position. However, it appears things can be rocky after just one game. Let's take a deeper dive into what Dabo Swinney had to say about Clemson's quarterbacks after Week 1.

Following the team's 51-10 loss to the LSU Tigers, there were a lot of questions about why this happened. Clemson's offense struggled passing the football as starting quarterback Christopher Vizzina completed 10 of 16 passes for 83 yards and an interception. Backup Tait Reynolds would also see some action, completing 4 of 6 passes for 22 yards. Following the game, coach Dabo Swinney was asked about who will be the starting quarterback for next week's game, and he responded with the following:

"I don't know. Again, we've got to watch the tape and evaluate and we'll go from there… That's what I said coming into it. That's why I said, we didn't want to guarantee (Reynolds) would play, but it was pretty likely he was going to play So we needed to play games. Again, I wish we had a game or two where you can work the kinks out, but thats not the stick we drew. We've got some stuff on tape now, we've got some things in real live games that we can evaluate, and we'll go from there."

Ahead of the game, it was clear the quarterback situation was something Dabo Swinney was still trying to figure out. He appeared on The Stephen A. Smith Show on Mad Dog Sports Radio and said the following about the quarterback battle:

"The quarterback is the big question. I mean, you know, and we're all gonna see it in real time. Chris [Vizzina] is gonna be our starter, and he earned the job and he won it, but we have another kid [Reynolds] that's right there. And we're just, Stephen A., as you know, we don't get preseason games. We're the only level of football from Pee Wee to NFL where you don't get to go and get some live preseason games. So our live preseason game is in Baton Rouge versus LSU. I've got confidence in these guys."

The starting quarterback situation between Chris Vizzina and Tait Reynolds is going to be something to keep an eye on throughout the season. It will be intriguing to see if one of them will be able to showcase their skills and take a firm grip on the Clemson Tigers' starting quarterback battle.

title: Analyst dubs Jared Verse as player to watch for Browns in 2026
description: Jared Verse is going to have a lot of eyes on him in his debut season as a Brown.
fullText:
The Browns' defense lost the best player in the NFL, according to those within the league, when they traded away Myles Garrett. The picks they got back will help in the future, but right now they will be relying on the presence of Jared Verse, who they also got back in the deal.

In the mind of ESPN's Benjamin Solak, he thinks Verse is going to be a difference-maker, one way or another, in 2026. While listing x-factors, Solak chose the Browns' new pass rusher.

He writes, "The next step for Verse is converting his high pressure rate (15.3% by Next Gen Stats' model, 10th among all edge rushers over the past two seasons) into sacks. Verse's pressure-to-sack ratio is only 8.4% -- fourth lowest among all edge rushers over the same time frame. The Browns' defense needs field-flipping plays to create winning environments for their offense, so Verse's pressures are insufficient. He can deliver the ceiling-raising impact of his predecessor only with a leap forward in sack production."

While no one can replace Garrett, Verse is still one of the best pass rushers in the NFL, and the x-factor he brings goes well beyond 2026.

title: Goodell Contract Extended After $270B Team Value Gain Since 2006
description: Roger Goodell reached an agreement on a four-year contract extension, the league announced Sunday. The deal runs through March 2031 and would mark 25 seasons with Goodell in charge, if he completes the contract. The compensation committee headed by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft informed the full ownership regarding the extension. The memo, reviewed …
fullText:
Roger Goodell reached an agreement on a four-year contract extension, the league announced Sunday. The deal runs through March 2031 and would mark 25 seasons with Goodell in charge, if he completes the contract.

The compensation committee headed by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft informed the full ownership regarding the extension. The memo, reviewed by Sportico, said the committee worked with a third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to "structure a deal that aligns Roger's compensation with the League's long-term interests and success." The value of the deal was not disclosed, but the memo stated that it is bonus heavy with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Goodell's and the NFL's performance measured against certain metrics.

New Seahawks Investors Include Warriors LP Who Shoved Kyle Lowry

Don't Wear Loud Versace If You're Losing: The Codes of Sports Styling

Kalshi Stops Its Sports Injury Betting Markets at CFTC's Request

"We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years," read the memo. The committee also includes John Mara (New York Giants), Shad Khan (Jacksonville Jaguars), Jimmy Haslam (Cleveland Browns), Michael Bidwell (Arizona Cardinals) and Greg Penner (Denver Broncos).

This is the fifth extension for Goodell, who took over for Paul Tagliabue in September 2006 after prevailing over Gregg Levy in what was a tight vote in the initial rounds of ballots. Goodell will be 72 when his new contract expires.

A major part of commissioner's role is to absorb the criticisms directed at the league and make ownership money. Goodell has checked both boxes during his career, including the 2011 lockout, a concussion settlement, the national anthem kneeling controversy and more.

On the financial front, the average NFL team was worth about $900 million, or $29 billion collectively, when Goodell took over in 2006. Sportico's NFL team valuations last month had the average at $9.34 billion and $299 billion total.

The least valuable NFL team is the Cincinnati Bengals at $7.4 billion. There are only six sports franchises on the planet outside the NFL that are worth more than the Bengals. The list includes three from the NBA, two in MLB and LaLiga's Real Madrid. The NFL's TV might is unmatched, with the latest round of media deals worth $125 billion over 11 years.

Investors have significantly re-priced how they look at sports teams, including those in the NFL. They are an asset class now, with the blessing of institutional investors that have poured into sports, seeking non-correlated assets, AI-proof investments, and one of the last things that broadcasters can command big dollars for from advertisers

The average NFL team was valued at a revenue multiple of 4.7 when Goodell became commissioner. (Revenue multiples are the standard valuation metric most bankers and investors use.) The multiple was 12.7 in Sportico's recent NFL valuations.

Goodell's compensation totaled $212.5 million during his first 10 years at the helm when the NFL was registered as a non-profit and had to disclose executive pay. Goodell's salary has not been disclosed since, but he made nearly $128 million combined for the 2019 and 2020 seasons, according to the New York Times.

If Goodell's yearly comp dipped after that to an average of $55 million, his total earnings from the NFL would reach roughly $1 billion by March 2031.

title: Guardians’ Stephen Vogt reveals reason behind Jose Ramirez’s removal from starting lineup
description: The Cleveland Guardians have decided to remove third baseman Jose Ramirez from the starting nine.
fullText:
The Cleveland Guardians are managing two lineup concerns heading into the final stretch of the regular season. Rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter is dealing with a right wrist sprain while veteran third baseman Jose Ramirez received a planned day off Sunday against the Detroit Tigers.

DeLauter suffered the wrist injury during the second game of Friday's doubleheader, feeling discomfort on his final swing of the night after being struck in the arm. The 24-year-old is day to day and the Guardians will monitor his progress before determining when he returns to the lineup.

MORE: MLB home plate umpire suddenly leaves National League game after passing out

In his first full big-league season, DeLauter has been one of Cleveland's most productive young players. Across 445 plate appearances he has posted a .294 batting average, .365 on-base percentage, .823 OPS, 13 home runs, 60 RBIs and 10 stolen bases. He went 2-for-3 with two doubles in the opener of Friday's doubleheader before the wrist issue emerged in the nightcap.

Ramirez's absence was precautionary. The 33-year-old has been managed carefully since returning from left hamate bone surgery earlier this season.

Across 119 games Ramirez has posted a .237 batting average, .330 on-base percentage and .708 OPS with 11 home runs, 48 RBIs and 31 stolen bases. Getting him off his feet for a day with the stretch run ahead is a sensible move for a team protecting one of its most important players.

The Guardians currently hold the final American League wild card spot and will need both players contributing down the stretch if they want to hold their position as September concludes.

title: Michigan’s stunning comeback could have big impact on Penn State
description: Michigan struggled in Week 1 despite its shocking Hail Mary win. The poor performance could create a path for Penn State to make the CFP.
fullText:
The Michigan Wolverines pulled off one of the most stunning wins in recent memory Saturday night. While there was some controversy surrounding the end-of-game scenario that added an extra second to the game clock and allowed them score a walk-off touchdown, the bigger story is that it happened against Western Michigan.

The Wolverines entered this year with one of the more talented rosters in college football, including five-star quarterback Bryce Underwood and four-star wide receiver Andrew Marsh. They began the season ranked No. 16 – two spots ahead of Penn State — but now that position will be reevaluated.

Michigan struggled mightily throughout the game, going scoreless for more than 50 minutes of game time before connecting on the Hail Mary. They ultimately pulled out the win, but that isn't the type of performance you want to put on the field against a far inferior opponent.

There is a chance the Nittany Lions will be ranked ahead of Michigan in the next AP Poll, and more importantly, that mid-October battle at The Big House could become the biggest game of the season. With the Wolverines being one of only three ranked teams that Penn State is slated to play this season, a win in that game could have significant implications on their College Football Playoff odds.

Obviously, we are only one game into the season, and a lot can change in the six weeks until that game. But with no clear powerhouses on the schedule, the Nittany Lions need to begin recalibrating what this season can look like if they take care of business.

Even if they get over the hump in Michigan, that game would only be the second in a month-long gauntlet that also sees the Blue and White take on USC and Washington. The games played between Oct. 10 and Nov. 7 will likely be the defining point of this Penn State season, and for right now, they appear to have the upper hand against at least one of those teams.

title: Oklahoma Sooners won't let Michigan result change preparation
description: The Oklahoma Sooners have a big road test in the Big House in Week 2 and won't let Michigan's performance change how they prepare.
fullText:
That's not the Michigan team the Oklahoma Sooners will face in Week 2.

Michigan survived, with some help from the replay officials, Western Michigan with a 13-12 win in Week 1. Bryce Underwood's second Hail Mary attempt was caught in the front of the end zone to give the Wolverines a one-point win.

Survive and advance is the name of the game.

Sure, Michigan didn't look great against the Broncos. They totaled just 276 yards, including just 106 on the ground against Western Michigan. The Wolverines were just 3 of 10 on third downs and had nine penalties for 80 yards in the win.

Not exactly the kind of performance you want to have before welcoming a top-10 team to your building.

But Michigan is better than that. Whether they took Western Michigan lightly or were overlooking them with OU coming to town next week, you know they'll be better for the Sooners and more prepared for what Brent Venables' crew wants to throw at them.

The good news for Oklahoma. They've been good on the road over the last couple of seasons. After falling short in road losses to Kansas and Oklahoma State in back-to-back weeks in 2023, the Sooners have performed better the last two seasons.

Even in the dreadful 2024 campaign, when Oklahoma struggled to do anything offensively, they beat Auburn on the road, led Ole Miss and LSU at halftime, and had Missouri beaten before letting it slip away in the final minutes. In 2025, the Sooners went on the road to beat South Carolina, Tennessee, and Alabama, three of the toughest places to play in the SEC.

Brent Venables has long preached an identity of playing to their own standard. Oklahoma isn't concerned with anything other than its own expectations.

You can bet they're not going to let Michigan's performance change the way they prepare for the Week 2 matchup. Because Brent Venables won't let them.

title: Aston Villa Eye £87m January Move For 20-Year-Old Striker: Why Should They Resist The Rush?
description: Aston Villa are preparing another move for a young forward after the summer window exposed how quickly their attacking options can change. Football Insider reporter Pete O’Rourke says Villa are keep...
fullText:
Aston Villa are preparing another move for a young forward after the summer window exposed how quickly their attacking options can change. Football Insider reporter Pete O'Rourke says Villa are keeping close tabs on Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane and could return with a January 2027 approach after failing to get a deal done before the deadline. Newcastle United have tracked the 20-year-old too, yet Villa see him as a possible long-term lead striker.

Kofane has built a strong profile since arriving at Leverkusen. He made 44 appearances in 2025/26, scoring seven goals and adding five assists, including five goals and four assists in 29 Bundesliga matches. He has started 2026/27 with two goals in two competitive appearances, scoring against Wehen Wiesbaden and SV Elversberg. Cameroon international Kofane scored twice at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Reports have placed a possible valuation near £87m, while summer bids reportedly reached €70m.

Villa don't strictly need another striker. Nicolas Jackson and Ibrahim Mbaye have strengthened the forward group, so Emery already has more options than he had after the summer reshuffle. Spending €40m-€70m on another expensive young attacker would therefore look like a luxury purchase rather than a response to a clear squad problem.

Kofane is exciting, though, and that matters. He offers a different physical presence, links play in short exchanges and attacks the box with intent. Former French player Samuel Lobe's comparison with Samuel Eto'o shows the level of potential some scouts see in him.

LEVERKUSEN, GERMANY – AUGUST 08: Christian Kofane of Bayer 04 Leverkusen enters the pitch prior to the pre-season friendly match between Bayer 04 Leverkusen and Sevilla FC at BayArena on August 08, 2026 in Leverkusen, Germany. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

The bigger issue sits behind the front three. Villa's scoring record has often exceeded their expected goals, so adding another finisher doesn't address the main weakness. Their defensive duel numbers have been a concern, with the squad previously winning only 59.32% of individual defensive phases. That points to a need for greater defensive strength and better security after losing possession.

Kofane can become a top striker, but January should serve immediate needs. Paying a huge fee for a player still developing, while competing with Watkins' replacement options for minutes, would stretch resources without fixing Villa's most pressing problem, especially with January funds better spent elsewhere. For Aston Villa, defensive steel looks more valuable right now, particularly in high-pressure Premier League matches this season.

title: Yordan Alvarez sets new career high during 142nd game with Astros
description: Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez is having an amazing season.
fullText:
Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez had an incredibly disappointing 2025 season. He dealt with a broken right hand as well as a left ankle sprain. Altogether, he played just 48 games that season.

He was fully healthy heading into the 2026 MLB season, and has gone right back to being one of the best hitters in the sport. His Astros team is making a more serious playoff push as well.

The team is 73-70, first place in the American League West and three games up on the second-place Texas Rangers. The two teams concluded their season series early in August, with the Astros taking it nine games to four.

MORE: Yankees facing predicament that could delay Aaron Judge's return

Aug 4, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez (44) bats during the third inning against the Toronto Blue Jays at Daikin Park. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

During Sunday's game against the Arizona Diamondbacks, the DH launched his 38th home run of the season. It was hit in the bottom of the first inning and gave the Astros a 1-0 lead in the series finale.

That home run helped him to eclipse his season high home run total which he set with 37 long balls in 2022. Alvarez made that happen in 135 games, and this one is his 142nd of the season.

At this rate, he will smash his personal record for most games played in a season (147 in 2024). To make that even sweeter, it could potentially be his first time winning the AL MVP award.

Alvarez is slashing .316/.434/.603 (1.037 OPS) with 38 home runs and 95 RBIs. To make those numbers even more impressive, he has just barely more strikeouts than walks on the season (108 to 99).

Alvarez's OPS is nearly 100 points higher than the next hitters closest to him, including the National League. He might be a primary DH, but with these hitting numbers he is currently the favorite to win AL MVP.

The next closest challenger is predictably Bobby Witt Jr. of the Kansas City Royals. His ability as a five-tool player always makes him an enticing option, but his hitting pails in comparison to Alvarez's this season.

title: Yamal hits double as 'nearly perfect' Barca thrash Valencia
description: Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100 percent start in La Liga.The reigning champions moved two points clear at the top of La Liga, after Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.
fullText:
Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100 percent start in La Liga.

The reigning champions moved two points clear at the top of La Liga, after Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

Unbeaten Alaves rose to second place with a thumping 5-2 victory over Osasuna.

As well as Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick's swaggering Barca on a hot afternoon on Spain's east coast.

Yamal did not take part in the team training session on Saturday after a knock but showed no signs of it during a dazzling display against Carlos Corberan's side.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia's fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium. Los Che are bottom and yet to win this season.

"We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team," said Flick.

"We stay calm and then if it's possible to score we try to do it -- it was a fantastic game for us.

"Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it's perfect then you can stop working."

Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Lopez dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star.

The 19-year-old slammed home at the near post for what he thought was Barca's second goal but the goal was disallowed for a tight offside after a VAR review.

Lopez netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up.

Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric Garcia had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with team-mate Rodri's shoulder, on the midfielder's first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.

Yamal fired narrowly wide and Lopez struck the post as Flick's side continued to dominate. Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia made a smart save to thwart Arnaut Danjuma at his near post before the break.

Raphinha, starting again as the team's centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Lopez fed him.

Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona's fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo.

New arrival Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barca debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide.

Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barca's fifth and conclude a profitable afternoon for both the World Cup winner and the Catalan giants.

"We have a very young team, with the right transfers we made, but it's the beginning of the season, it's not the end," added Flick, telling his team not to get too excited yet about their strong start.

"We have to go a long, long way."

Corberan said his team were up against it from the start after Yamal's rapid strike.

"Conceding a goal so early, on their first or second attack, made everything much more difficult," said the Valencia coach.

"It's a difficult situation that we will navigate together."

Later on Sunday Lucas Boye bagged a hat-trick for Alaves as they crushed Osasuna 5-2, with two of his efforts coming from long range.

Former Real Madrid striker Mariano Diaz and Pablo Ibanez also scored for Quique Sanchez Flores's team, while Ante Budimir grabbed two for Osasuna, who fell to their first defeat.

"I hope we don't take our foot off the gas and we stay in this dynamic, which will take us far," said Boye.

"This is a humble team and we will go game by game."

title: Arizona’s Geraldo Perdomo leaves game after being hit in the helmet by a line drive
description: Arizona’s Geraldo Perdomo left Sunday’s game against the Houston Astros after being struck in the helmet by a line drive from Ketel Marte in the third inning.  Perdomo singled to start the third before Marte’s 93 mph single hit him on the side of the helmet as he ran to second.  Perdomo talked to trainers for a bit before being helped to his feet and walking off the field on his own power.
fullText:
HOUSTON (AP) — Arizona's Geraldo Perdomo left Sunday's game against the Houston Astros after being struck in the helmet by a line drive from Ketel Marte in the third inning.

Perdomo singled to start the third before Marte's 93 mph single hit him on the side of the helmet as he ran to second. He immediately fell to the ground and writhed in pain as players from both teams ran to check on him.

He remained on his back for a couple of minutes as trainers tended to him before he sat up. Perdomo talked to trainers for a bit before being helped to his feet and walking off the field on his own power.

Ildemaro Vargas moved from first base to shortstop in the bottom of the inning to replace Perdomo and Tim Tawa entered the game to play first base.

The team did not immediately provide details on Perdomo's condition.

title: NFL rankings: Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride 26th in ESPN player rankings
description: A look at where Trey McBride lands in ESPN's projected top 100 players for 2026.
fullText:
The Arizona Cardinals have arguably the best tight end in the NFL in Trey McBride. He was ranked No. 13 in the "NFL Top 100 Players of 2026," the player-voted player rankings.

ESPN put together a list of the projected top 100 players of 2026. Where does McBride rank?

Even on a team with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson, it's not entirely inconceivable that McBride is the Cardinals' top receiving option. He spent the offseason refining his ability to read the defense and understand his spacing, which will only make the player with the most routes run in 2025 even more dangerous in space. Throughout training camp, McBride has put his receiving ability on display, a skill that will be amplified in new coach Mike LaFleur's West Coast scheme. -- Josh Weinfuss

Signature stat: McBride's past two campaigns (126 receptions in 2025 and 111 receptions in 2024) rank first and fifth, respectively, among tight ends all time. He's the only tight end in NFL history with 100-plus receptions in back-to-back seasons.

No. 26 isn't a bad ranking. However, the weird thing are his projected stats. The projections say he will catch 149 passes for only 1,023 yards and five touchdowns. He has a career 10.0 yards per reception. Why would he suddenly drop to 6.9 yards, especially when head coach Mike LaFleur believes McBride could have more George Kittle-like production, and Kittle has a career 13.5-yard per-catch average.

What would be more reasonable for a projection for McBride, especially with Wilson and Harrison getting more targets, is 95 catches for 1,150 yards.

title: 5 fun facts: Get to know Nets' Mikel Brown Jr. ahead of 2026-27 season
description: As the sixth pick in the draft, guard Mikel Brown Jr. joins the Nets after a stellar freshman campaign at Louisville.
fullText:
As the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft, guard Mikel Brown Jr. joins the Brooklyn Nets after a stellar freshman campaign at Louisville.

Brown was named to the All-ACC third team, averaging 18.2 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 34.4% from 3-point range. He dropped a career-high 45 points on Feb. 9, tying the single-game program scoring record (Wes Unseld).

The 20-year-old was limited to 21 games due to a back injury that sidelined him in the middle of the season and during the postseason. However, he was still one of 15 players in the ACC to register 10 or more games with at least five assists.

Brown became the Cardinals' highest-drafted player since Felton Spencer was selected sixth overall in 1990. He was the first top-10 pick from Louisville since 1996 (Samaki Walker, No. 9) and the school's first first-round pick since Donovan Mitchell in 2017.

The 6-foot-5 Brown debuted with the Nets in summer league, averaging 15 points, four assists, 1.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 34.6% from 3-point range in four games. He finished in double figures in each appearance, including a 20-point performance on July 10.

Brown is eager to get to work and hit the court with his teammates for the first time. He wants to impact winning above all else and help the Nets turn things around on the court.

Previous: AJ Dybantsa | Darryn Peterson | Cameron Boozer | Caleb Wilson | Keaton Wagler

Brown grew up with parents who also played college basketball. His father, Christopher Sr., played at West Florida, and his mother, Marisela, played at St. Petersburg College. He has often said that his father had the greatest influence on his athletic career.

Brown has plenty of off-court hobbies, but it might be fishing that is his favorite. He considers himself a "big fisherman" and guesses that the biggest fish he has ever caught is a 10-pound largemouth bass.

Brown wore No. 0 at his various stops in high school and for one season at Louisville as a nod to All-Stars Damian Lillard and Russell Westbrook, who have donned it throughout their Hall of Fame careers. He will continue that trend with the Nets.

"I chose it in like fourth or fifth grade," Brown said, via the NBA on Instagram. "I kind of just went with the number because I liked Damian Lillard and Russell Westbrook at the time, and I still do. It is going to be surreal to go up against (Damian). I remember talking about it a couple of years ago, and he told me he expects me to be here soon, so I'm here now."

Brown recently revealed that 16-year veteran Rajon Rondo served as a mentor for him last season at Louisville. After studying him as he grew up, Brown had the opportunity to learn and seek advice from Rondo, which he said proved invaluable throughout the year.

"I was fortunate enough to have him as a mentor this year," Brown said on "Cousins" with Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady in July. "He was in Louisville. He invited me to his crib, and we watched some film together; played a little bit of chess. I got to pick his brain a lot this year, watch film with him. … He broke the game down in just such a simple way. He just kept telling me, 'You don't need to overcomplicate it. You're extremely talented. Just keep it simple, and I promise you, you're going to make the right play every single time.'"

Brown was named the 2025 USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year after helping the United States to the gold medal in the 2025 FIBA U19 World Cup. Playing alongside the likes of AJ Dybantsa, Morez Johnson Jr. and Koa Peat, Brown averaged 14.9 points, 6.1 assists and 2.1 rebounds in seven appearances. He also won a gold medal in the 2024 FIBA U18 AmeriCup.

title: Oregon LB Dylan Williams seizes opportunity in win over Boise State
description: Dylan Williams wasn't circled as a key contributor before Week 1, but the junior linebacker played an vital role in Oregon's victory over Boise State.
fullText:
Entering the first game of the season against Boise State, the Oregon Ducks didn't have many pressing questions defensively. Rather, there were expectations of growth and maturity from the unit's various returning leaders.

In the season opener, the Ducks saw some of the improvement they hoped for. The defensive line closed the game out with relentless pressure. The secondary, although caught for penalties at times, held Boise State's passing attack in check in key spots, and safety Koi Perich led the team with 11 tackles.

Jerry Mixon Jr. and Devon Jackson were expected to command the linebacker room and lead the defense as well. While the veteran pair did share the field often, junior linebacker Dylan Williams was an unexpected bright spot in the 34-27 victory.

Williams, a former four-star recruit from Los Angeles, did not see the field often in his first two seasons in Eugene. He primarily contributed on special teams and late in blowout games while he progressed toward what Dan Lanning and the Oregon coaching staff envisioned for him. On Saturday, the Ducks got a very good look at Williams' progression.

Although he was only credited with a pair of tackles and half a tackle for loss, Williams was excellent when defending the run. He saw the rushing lanes for Boise State's dynamic duo in the backfield and altered the route enough to create negative plays.

The performance earned Williams more snaps as the game went along, including in big moments late in the fourth quarter. Lanning wasn't surprised by Williams' sudden breakout, and it likely won't be the last time we see him making plays in the middle of Oregon's defense.

"He's certainly earned it in fall camp," Lanning said of Williams. "He's worked extremely hard to put himself in position. He's made a lot of plays in fall camp, and there are certainly moments today, as you're watching as a coach, you're like, 'Let's continue to figure out how to get that guy on the field and utilize his skill set.'"

As the game wore on, Williams earned opportunities to share the field with Jackson, taking Mixon's spot. After losing the defense's leading tackler the past two seasons in Bryce Boettcher, the Ducks appear to have three capable defenders in the heart of the defense to replace him.

A blue-chip recruit that doesn't see the field in his first two seasons is typically a candidate to hit the transfer portal. Instead, Williams stuck around. Having been able to watch and learn from Boettcher, Mixon and Jackson, he's now proving the time on the sideline wasn't wasted.

"I'm proud of Dylan's growth," Lanning said. "He's a guy that stuck through it. He's had limited opportunities up until this year, but I'm anticipating Dylan having a big year for us and growing from the moments that he had today."

title: Yamal scores twice as Barcelona wins 4th straight game in La Liga, Arsenal beats Chelsea
description: Barcelona stayed perfect in the Spanish league by cruising to a 5-0 win at Valencia on Sunday, with Lamine Yamal scoring another brace for the Catalan club.  Arsenal rallied to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the Premier League, while Manchester United was stunned in added time to draw 2-2 at Everton.  Augsburg moved to the top of the Bundesliga by winning 4-1 at Eintracht Frankfurt, and American midfielder Giovanni Reyna scored in Strasbourg's 6-2 rout of Troyes in France.
fullText:
MADRID (AP) — Barcelona stayed perfect in the Spanish league by cruising to a 5-0 win at Valencia on Sunday, with Lamine Yamal scoring another brace for the Catalan club.

Arsenal rallied to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the Premier League, while Manchester United was stunned in added time to draw 2-2 at Everton.

Augsburg moved to the top of the Bundesliga by winning 4-1 at Eintracht Frankfurt, and American midfielder Giovanni Reyna scored in Strasbourg's 6-2 rout of Troyes in France.

Barcelona won its fourth game in a row at the start of the Spanish league and is the only team with a perfect record after four rounds.

Yamal scored a goal in each half following his first two goals of the season in the win against Rayo Vallecano in the previous round.

Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri also found the net for Barcelona, which has outscored opponents 17-2 in four games.

Midfielder Rodri made his first start since joining Barcelona from Manchester City, and newly signed forward Gabriel Jesus came off the bench in the second half for his Barcelona debut.

Defender Eric García had to be replaced in the first half after being struck in the face in a collision with Rodri.

Valencia lost its third in a row. It has scored only once in four matches. The home rout sparked protests by Valencia fans, who gathered in large numbers outside the Mestalla Stadium after the match.

Arsenal joined Man City at the top of the standings in England by coming from behind to defeat Chelsea in its biggest test so far in its title defense.

Martin Odegaard scored a 50th-minute winner after Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea an early lead and Kai Havertz equalized for Chelsea in the first half.

Arsenal has won its first three Premier league matches. It was Chelsea's first loss after two opening wins.

Man United, which has only one victory in three league games, conceded a stoppage-time goal to draw with Everton after twice holding the lead.

Deadline-day signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles came off the bench to make his debut and score a long-range shot into the top corner to salvage a point for his new club.

Reyna got his first goal with Strasbourg in his new club's trouncing of Troyes.

The 23-year-old U.S. international joined Strasbourg from Borussia Monchengladbach.

Sam Amo-Ameyaw added a pair of late goals for the visitors, which have won two in a row after a 4-0 opening loss at Marseille. Troyes had taken the lead with Antoine Mille in the ninth minute and stayed ahead until Jacobo Ortega's 40th-minute equalizer.

Rennes won 2-1 at Angers for its second victory in three rounds.

Augsburg conceded six minutes into the match but scored four unanswered goals in the second half to defeat Eintracht Frankfurt.

Augsburg's second straight win saw the club go top of the standings on goal difference. Three other teams have also won two matches to start the season — Freiburg, Borussia Dortmund and Elversberg.

Also Sunday, Mainz routed Hamburger 5-0 on the road.

title: Recap: Bayern Munich Frauen set oust SC Freiburg 4-1
description: Men, this is how you score goals.
fullText:
Bayern Munich Frauen picked up another win with a 4-1 victory over SC Freiburg. Bayern have now officially gone 45 games without defeat in the Bundesliga, a new league record

The German record champions were coming off the back of three straight wins in all competitions, and were not about to stop today. In the 18th minute, Momoko Tanikawa scored a candidate for Goal of the Season when she saw the keeper off her line, and unleashed a long range shot from the halfway line that sailed into the net.

Vanessa Gilles then added a second goal by finishing a Klara Bühl free kick. It was her second goal in as many games.

Bayern momentarily lost a bit of control after the restart and let Freiburg pull one back through German youth international Luca-Emily Birkholz in the 64th minute. However, they immediately regrouped and regained their two-goal advantage 12 minutes later. Lena Oberdorf registered her first assist of the season with a pinpoint through ball to Bühl, who rounded the keeper and finished.

There was still time for Tanikawa to get her second of the afternoon after receiving a pass from Bühl and driving the ball into the bottom corner from just outside the box. Bühl thus got her second assist of the game in stoppage time.

There was also more reason to celebrate as Sophie Proost got her first competitive start for Bayern, while Sarah Zadrazil made her long awaited return from her ACL injury, which also happened against Freiburg of all teams.

The result brings Bayern joint-top of the Bundesliga, just behind VfL Wolfsburg on goals scored. Bayern's next game is another Monday game, when they visit Bayer Leverkusen next week.

title: Western Michigan president wanted a way to appeal decision, 'but there is none'
description: Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna told reporters on Sunday that the Broncos won't appeal the controversial end to Week 1 game vs. Michigan.
fullText:
Western Michigan will not appeal the controversial ending to its Week 1 loss to Michigan.

It won't be for a lack of effort, though.

Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Sept. 6, Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna said he explored looking into the Broncos' options but ultimately will not pursue an appeal after officials put one second back on the clock in the closing moments of Saturday's game. The decision gave Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood one final snap, which he turned into a game-winning 47-yard Hail Mary touchdown pass for the Wolverines.

HAYES: Michigan football lost to Western Michigan. Then the Big Ten stepped in | Opinion

"I did want to find a way to appeal that decision, but there is none," Kavalhuna said alongside Western Michigan coach Lance Taylor at Sunday's press conference.

"I've looked into this pretty closely. I used to be a federal prosecutor. I don't discern anything unfair or untoward in this process," Kavalhuna added.

The controversy stems from the final play — and second — on Saturday's game at The Big House in Ann Arbor when Underwood's previous Hail Mary attempt sailed out of the back of the end zone as the clock at the stadium went triple zeros. However, the game didn't end there.

Following a review, officials put one second back on the clock, giving the Wolverines their opportunity to win — and avoid a loss that would have cost $1.5 million, as that is how much they reportedly paid the Broncos for the game.

"Ultimately the refs did not cost this game and if we make the mistake of making an excuse, it allows us to be bitter instead of getting better, and I think that that's (not) where we want to where we want to go as a football team," Taylor said during Sunday's press conference.

REQUIRED READING: Big Ten explains Michigan Hail Mary decision, MAC accepts it

The Big Ten defended the decision in a post-game statement.

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling," the Big Ten said in a statement.

The Big Ten also cited Rule 4-2-3-a from the NCAA Football Rulebook, which states: "A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside a boundary line."

In a different statement late Saturday night, MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher mentioned that Western Michigan officials and he reached out to the Big Ten after the game, and that the Big Ten explained and confirmed the decision to add a second.

Michigan will host Oklahoma in Week 2 for a top-25 matchup, while Western Michigan will host Monmouth University on Saturday, Sept. 12.

Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast, hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify.

title: Pundit believes Liverpool could make move for Real Madrid legend
description: Liverpool Transfer Latest: Dani Carvajal Link Emerges as Lamine Camara Continues to Impress ScoutsLiverpool’s squad planning continues to attract attention, with activity at right-back, midfield and...
fullText:
Liverpool's squad planning continues to attract attention, with activity at right-back, midfield and in the long-term goalkeeping department all feeding into the wider picture around Anfield. There is a familiar theme running through it all, Liverpool are trying to balance immediate needs with the next phase of their rebuild under Andoni Iraola.

One of the more eye-catching developments comes via Joleon Lescott on TNT Sports, where the former defender said, "I think there's talk of Liverpool, Carvajal, right-back. So, yeah, I would say Liverpool as well." It is a striking suggestion given Dani Carvajal's standing in the game and his experience at the highest level, even if any deal would clearly be outside the usual transfer-window rhythm.

Liverpool did address important areas during the summer, bringing in Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo after defensive injuries created a pressing issue, while Bradley Barcola added another high-end option in attack. Yet concerns around the full-back positions have not gone away, particularly on the right.

With Conor Bradley and Joe Gomez dealing with injury issues, Jeremie Frimpong has largely stood alone as the senior option there. That lack of depth has naturally encouraged speculation, and Carvajal's name has now entered the conversation. At 34, the former Real Madrid defender would bring a wealth of know-how, personality and game management. Any serious interest would hinge on fitness, readiness and whether Liverpool view a short-term solution as worthwhile while injuries persist.

From a recruitment perspective, it would be an opportunistic move rather than a conventional one. Liverpool have often tried to think several windows ahead, but elite experience can still hold appeal when a squad needs stability in a specialist role.

In midfield, Lamine Camara is a name that has not gone away. Liverpool tracked him in the summer and remain among the clubs with a close eye on his development, alongside Chelsea. Monaco resisted late pressure previously, despite advanced movement elsewhere, and that has ensured the race may simply have been delayed rather than ended.

Scouts from Liverpool and other Premier League clubs were present as Monaco defeated Paris Saint-Germain 2-1 on Friday, and Camara's display appears to have further strengthened his reputation. His work against a technically strong PSG midfield carried real weight. Containing players of the level of Joao Neves, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz speaks to the tactical discipline and physical output he would need in England.

Liverpool's midfield is not an area of emergency, but it is one where succession planning matters. Camara fits the profile of a player who could grow into a major role over time, and the fact top clubs continue to monitor him so closely suggests this is one to revisit in 2027.

From a Liverpool perspective, this all feels a little mixed. The Carvajal link is interesting on paper, but it also raises a blunt question, why has the squad been left needing this kind of fix in the first place? If Liverpool are seriously looking at a 34-year-old free agent at right-back, that suggests the planning around depth has not been as clean as it should have been.

Camara, meanwhile, sounds like exactly the sort of player supporters can get excited about, but there is always a danger in building too much around scouting reports and future windows. Liverpool need quality now as well as promise later. Watching a midfielder shine against PSG is one thing, getting a deal done against rival interest is another.

As for Brughmans, the talent may be obvious, though goalkeeper deals for teenagers always require caution. Big fees and long timelines can create a lot of noise before a player is anywhere near ready for Liverpool's first team.

Supporters will probably see the logic in each individual story, but taken together they also hint at a club still juggling short-term patchwork with long-term ambition. That balance can work, though only if the immediate team does not keep drifting into avoidable gaps.
