title: TreVeyon Henderson injury update doesn't bode well for Pats RB's Week 1 status
description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was once again absent from practice on Sunday. Here's the latest injury update on the Patriots running back.
fullText:
TreVeyon Henderson injury update doesn't bode well for Pats RB's Week 1 status originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New England Patriots were back on the practice field Sunday as they prepare for the Week 1 contest against the Seattle Seahawks and all eyes were once again on the lookout for running back TreVeyon Henderson.

Henderson hasn't practiced since Aug. 24 after coming down with an ankle injury.

With just days to go before the season-opener on Wednesday night, here's the latest report on Henderson's status from practice on Sunday.

According to Alex Barth of 98.5 The Sports Hub, Henderson was once again not at practice on Sunday. Christian Barmore and Ben Brown were also not present.

"Christian Barmore is a new absence at Patriots practice today. TreVeyon Henderson and Ben Brown are also not on the field," Barth reported.

On Saturday, head coach Mike Vrabel hinted that Henderson could return to practice, but that never came to fruition, and the same was the case on Sunday.

The Patriots will release their first injury report of the season later in the day, but for now Henderson's Week 1 status continues to be in doubt.

If Henderson doesn't play in Week 1, we would expect a heavy dose of Rhamondre Stevenson, who ESPN's Mike Reiss labeled the clear lead back in New England.

Reiss goes on to note that the Pats only have one other running back on their 53-man roster in Corey Kiner, but New England will certainly elevate another back from the practice squad, whether that be Hassan Haskins or Lan Larison.

Haskins has the edge if the Pats want a more experienced player, but Reiss adds that Larison could get the call if New England is more worried about having someone who is more familiar with Josh McDaniels' system.

"Larison gets the edge in terms of background in coordinator Josh McDaniels' system (critical with pass protection in mind), while Haskins would be the pick if NFL experience (44 games) was deemed a priority. Both factor into the mix on special teams, especially on punt protection, which is an area the Patriots have spent countless hours practicing throughout the summer," Reiss said.

No matter who is elevated, Stevenson is going to see plenty of work if Henderson is sidelined, and we'd expect a mix of Kiner and one of the other two backs to spell him.

title: Two right-backs in midfield - are Chelsea short despite £349m spent?
description: Chelsea ended Sunday's 2-1 defeat by champions Arsenal with two right-backs alongside each other in midfield - how did they get here?
fullText:
Chelsea ended Sunday's 2-1 defeat by champions Arsenal with two players who began their careers as right-backs alongside each other in midfield.

After spending £349m during the summer transfer window, how did they reach that point?

It was Reece James, who began his career as a right-back, who failed to track captain Martin Odegaard as he scored Arsenal's winner at Emirates Stadium.

In the build-up to his first defeat as Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso said he believes James can become one of the best midfielders in the world.

James performed well otherwise and spent almost half of last season playing in midfield.

But there are legitimate questions about Chelsea's depth in that area after Malo Gusto replaced midfielder Romeo Lavia in the second half.

It was lax marking that led to Odegaard's winner, while a lack of creativity from the bench left Chelsea short as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta's substitutes ultimately helped guide the hosts to victory.

"Chelsea don't have European football this season so they're playing less games and can concentrate on the Premier League. But the worry is you're finishing a game against the champions, and you've got two right-backs in midfield," Ashley Young told BBC Sport.

"You look at Lavia, who was injured a lot last season. The front line are going to send fear throughout the league but behind that you see the midfield and they're playing right-backs there.

"Teams will be seeing the game today, seeing that Chelsea will sit in there and get men behind the ball, but there's still spaces through the lines, and Arsenal found that out.

"Chelsea are giving up a lot of possession and they're playing counter-attacking football. Today there was probably only once with [Pedro] Neto down the right side when they capitalised on the counter."

The primary issue is the absence of midfielder Moises Caicedo.

The Ecuador international is out with an unspecified injury for an unknown period after breaking down just 11 minutes into a substitute appearance against Brighton last week.

It has left Alonso in almost uncharted territory for a Chelsea boss. Aside from suspensions, Caicedo had missed only two matches during the previous three seasons, through a knock and illness.

Asked about Caicedo, Alonso said: "Not longer term, but it is about assessing the risk. Probably last week we brought him back too early and I don't want to make the same mistake again."

It remains unclear whether Chelsea had concerns over Caicedo's fitness while pursuing several central midfielders on transfer deadline day.

Monaco pulled the plug on Chelsea's £47m move for Lamine Camara at the last minute, leaving officials at Stamford Bridge furious.

Chelsea also had bids of up to £64m rejected for Bournemouth's Alex Scott earlier in the summer and were prevented from signing France international Manu Kone after Roma head coach Gian Piero Gasperini blocked the move.

Chelsea said they pursued Camara because of a market opportunity, adding that they were satisfied with their summer business and retained faith in their current options.

That was despite selling Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint British-record fee of £125m on deadline day, without signing a direct replacement.

However, Caicedo's absence means he joins Jordan Henderson on the sidelines, with the England international still recovering from a broken arm suffered after falling over an advertising hoarding while an unused substitute at the World Cup.

Natural midfielder Valentin Barco, who joined from Strasbourg in the summer, has been overlooked in favour of Gusto in all three of Chelsea's Premier League matches.

With Gusto starting in midfield, Chelsea recorded 25.6% possession in last weekend's 4-3 victory over Brighton, their lowest figure since records began in 2003-04.

If all of Chelsea's midfield options are fit, and Caicedo's injury proves only minor, they should be able to cope with five midfielders in a season without midweek European football, as Alonso argued before the match.

Chelsea have leaned on their star attackers in Morgan Rogers, a resurgent Cole Palmer and the prolific Joao Pedro in their opening three matches.

Yet having conceded seven goals in three matches, Alonso said "we want to be tighter".

There was still plenty to admire about Chelsea's performance.

Club-record signing Rogers scored again in the second minute, becoming the first Chelsea player to score or assist in each of the club's opening three Premier League matches of a season since Eden Hazard in 2018-19.

It was arguably one of Chelsea's better performances against Arsenal during a run of 10 matches without a win against their London rivals.

There remains a 33-point gap to make up after Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League last season.

Alonso said after the match: "We came to win. We knew that we were not that far, but it went their way.

"It hurts, [we're] disappointed for sure. But this is the first defeat, this is going to be a long way and it doesn't have a big impact in our mood and in our mindset."

Arsenal remain the benchmark Chelsea are trying to reach. Although the Blues beat them to the signing of Rogers, they still trail the standard-setters in London and the Premier League.

It served to highlight that, despite already recruiting 10 first-team players during a busy summer, Chelsea's failure to sign a midfielder on deadline day may have left them with a potential weakness.

Alonso described the summer as "phase one" earlier this week. If Caicedo's return does not resolve Chelsea's midfield issues, the club may face questions over its decision not to sign a replacement for Fernandez before turning back to the market in January.

title: Matthew Stafford is fantastic in international games
description: Both times he’s gone overseas, Stafford has put on a show.
fullText:
When the Los Angeles Rams take the field in Melbourne this week against the San Francisco 49ers, it will feel somewhat like home for quarterback Matthew Stafford, even though they'll be playing several thousand miles from L.A.

Stafford has played in a pair of international games during his long career, and both times he's put up performances to remember.

Last year, Stafford led the way in a dominant 35-7 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in the Jags' second home, London. It was bizarre game for the Rams, box score-wise, considering they only tallied 271 yards but scored five touchdowns.

All five of those touchdowns, in fact, came from the right arm of the NFL's Most Valuable Player. While only averaging 5.5 yards per attempt and racking up 182 total passing yards, Stafford hit Davante Adams for three scores, plus one apiece for Terrance Ferguson and Konata Mumpfield.

One of the most impressive parts of the win and Stafford's effort in particular is the fact the Rams didn't have first-team All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua available in the game. Without him, Stafford completed passes to 10 different receivers and Los Angeles cruised to a victory last October.

Matthew Stafford faced a season-high 55.9% blitz rate against the Jaguars and threw all five of his touchdowns against the blitz.

Stafford tied Patrick Mahomes and Baker Mayfield for the most TD passes against the blitz in any game since 2016.#LARvsJAX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/kkDwSMpf5B

You have to go over a decade back in time to get to Stafford's other international appearance, a legendary comeback for the Detroit Lions over the Atlanta Falcons.

Two full seasons before the notorious collapse in the history of football, the Falcons led the Lions 21-0 at the half in London. Atlanta wouldn't score again, however, while Stafford engineered one of his NFL-high five fourth-quarter comebacks that season. Along with three field goals from Matt Prater, including the game winner as time expired, Stafford connected with Golden Tate in the third quarter and Theo Riddick in the fourth for touchdowns as part of the comeback effort.

That was one of Stafford's best seasons in Detroit, earning a Pro Bowl nod while leading the Lions to the postseason, a rarity at the time for that franchise. That game, in particular, was one of the biggest moments of that campaign.

Ideally, this would be a harbinger of things to come for the Rams this week, but considering past events don't dictate future outcomes (and neither of those games was completely on the opposite side of the world), this is probably little more than a pair of fun anecdotes.

But, if it helps you get some trash talk off this week, then it was all worth it.

title: Pierre Gasly's Monaco Podium Got Stripped Twice in Three Months, and the FIA's Reasoning Is a Wake-Up Call for Every Team
description: Pierre Gasly finished third at Monaco in June, lost the position to a pit lane penalty a few hours later, got it back five days after that on a technicality, and then lost it again this week when the FIA's International Court of Appeal overturned the reversal for good. Two five-second penalties, three rulings, and three months of paperwork later, the case says a lot more about how Formula 1 measures speed in the pit lane than it does about anything Gasly did wrong behind the wheel. A Podium Lost
fullText:
Pierre Gasly finished third at Monaco in June, lost the position to a pit lane penalty a few hours later, got it back five days after that on a technicality, and then lost it again this week when the FIA's International Court of Appeal overturned the reversal for good. Two five-second penalties, three rulings, and three months of paperwork later, the case says a lot more about how Formula 1 measures speed in the pit lane than it does about anything Gasly did wrong behind the wheel.

For the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix, the Race Director trimmed the standard 80 km/h pit lane speed limit down to 60 km/h, a nod to how tight the entry and exit are around the harbor. Formula One's Official Timing System doesn't clock instantaneous speed through that zone. It divides the pit lane into sectors bounded by paired timing loops embedded in the tarmac, then calculates each car's average speed between them using a distance figure that FOM measures by hand with a tape measure before the weekend even starts. Gasly's Alpine tripped two of those sectors at a calculated 60.4 km/h and 60.5 km/h, each worth a five-second penalty.

He wasn't alone. Six penalties for pit lane speeding went out that weekend across 423 pit lane passes, including one for teammate Franco Colapinto, who dropped out of the points entirely. Alpine chose to add both of Gasly's penalties to his race time after the fact rather than have him serve them under the safety car, and when the math landed, third place became seventh.

Within the deadline set by the International Sporting Code, Alpine petitioned for a Right of Review, arguing the loop-to-loop distance FOM had entered into the timing software wasn't the shortest path a car could actually take through that section of pit lane. A review petition only earns a hearing if the team can show a genuinely new element that wasn't available when the original penalty was issued, and Alpine cleared that bar because FOM itself flagged, three days after the race, that the entry loop measurement might not reflect the tightest realistic line through the corner. The Stewards agreed the information was new, then ruled on the merits that Gasly hadn't actually broken 60 km/h once a different, GPS-derived distance figure replaced the tape-measured one everybody had raced under. Both penalties were tossed and Gasly's third place was restored on June 12, a decision that seemed to close the book on the whole affair.

It didn't close anything. McLaren and Red Bull Racing, neither of which had a driver directly involved in the penalty, appealed the Stewards' reversal to the International Court of Appeal, joined as third parties by Racing Bulls and backed procedurally by Motorsport UK. That's a useful reminder of how connected an F1 classification really is: reshuffling one car's race time doesn't just move Gasly, it moves every scoring position behind him, and both constructors evidently had enough riding on that ripple in the championship table to spend the money on a full appeal. Alpine, with the FIA itself defending the Stewards' ruling it had issued, argued the reversal was fair precisely because the original timing data had been shown to be unreliable.

After a hearing in Paris on August 25, the International Court of Appeal sided with McLaren and Red Bull Racing and reinstated both penalties on September 3. The panel's real problem wasn't whether Gasly's Alpine crossed 60 km/h. It was about which yardstick gets to answer that question after the fact. The Stewards had accepted an alternative pit lane distance that Alpine calculated from GPS data reconstructed after the race, on a street circuit that had already been dismantled, in place of the tape-measured figure every team had calibrated against all weekend. The Court held that once FOM sets and publishes that reference distance before a session, it has to stay fixed for the rest of the competition, because competitors made real strategic and technical decisions against that one number. Letting it move retroactively would hand an advantage to whichever team can produce the most favorable post-race recalculation.

It's a subtle distinction, but it effectively closes a loophole. A Right of Review can surface a genuinely new fact, like a broken sensor or a miscommunication nobody caught in real time, but it can't be used to swap out the measurement method itself once the race is run and every car's setup is locked in against the original numbers.

The ruling forces a recalculation of both the Drivers' and Constructors' Championship points from Monaco onward, with Gasly back to seventh. According to Formula 1's own account of the reshuffled standings, Isack Hadjar inherits the third-place trophy he never got to stand on in June, a small mercy in what has otherwise been a rollercoaster rookie season for the Red Bull driver. The FIA and Alpine will split the appeal costs down the middle, while McLaren, Red Bull Racing, and Racing Bulls get their appeal deposits refunded, standard practice in FIA proceedings meant to discourage frivolous appeals but returned here because the Appellants won.

For engineers, the case is a reminder that pit lane compliance gets judged against whatever number FOM taped down before Thursday practice, not whatever a team's own GPS logger says on Sunday night, a distinction worth building into setup and strategy calls at every street circuit on the calendar, including Singapore and Las Vegas later this year. For fans, it's a reminder that a Formula 1 result isn't fully final until the appeal windows run out, and those windows can stretch across an entire summer.

Monaco has now become as reliable a source of courtroom drama as it is of processional racing, and Gasly, who spent the back half of his season fighting through midfield chaos at races like the British Grand Prix, has lost the same podium finish twice without changing a single lap of how he actually drove it.

title: Jon Sumrall praises offense, challenges defense after FAU win
description: Jon Sumrall discussed Aaron Philo's debut, Jadan Baugh's explosive performance and areas Florida must improve after its season-opening win over FAU.
fullText:
Florida football coach Jon Sumrall met with reporters following the Gators' season-opening win over FAU on Saturday night.

Sumrall evaluated Aaron Philo's debut as Florida's starting quarterback, Jadan Baugh's explosive performance and an offense that produced 66 points and 624 yards. He also praised Vernell Brown III, D.J. Coleman and the Gators' perimeter blocking.

The first-year Florida coach was less satisfied with his defense, saying the unit has plenty to correct despite the lopsided victory. Sumrall also discussed his first Gator Walk, running onto Florida Field and the importance of continuing to develop the team's younger players.

Here's everything Sumrall had to say.

Glad to be 1-0 and happy for our guys. It was fun watching a lot of our production tonight. I thought the guys came into the game with the right mindset and the right approach.

They were prepared. They didn't take the opportunity for granted. They were emotionally charged and ready to go. There is a lot to clean up. It was by no means a perfect performance. There is a long list of things we have to get a lot better at if we have high goals here.

I'm grateful for the fans. Unbelievable turnout and energy. It was electric. I got asked a little bit ago about running out of the tunnel for the first time. It surpassed my expectations, and I had pretty high expectations of what it was going to be like. What an unbelievable crowd and great support. They had a huge impact on the game. We need that each and every week, which I have no doubt we will.

I'm grateful for the guys' effort. There is a lot to work on and a lot to grow from. I told them just now that the journey of a thousand miles starts with a single step. That was step one. The goal this week was to be 1-0. We've got to go back to the drawing board and get a little bit better each day this week to keep improving.

I'm proud of him. He's prepared. He has worked really, really hard. He's an unbelievable teammate. He's a great leader. The game means a lot to him. I think he showed his comfortability by how he operated. He made good decisions for the most part with the football.

He was accurate. He distributed it well. I thought he did a really nice job. The interception really wasn't on him, to be quite honest with you. That ball should have been caught. I thought he played really well.

We're really young as a team. Jadan Baugh may not be young, but there were a lot of guys out there playing football who are just young.

I told the staff going into the game that we were going to be aggressive all night. We're not in any position to shut it down right now. We've got to figure out who the next guy up is and roll guys in. We weren't going to change how we played the game.

I'm very proud of Aaron. His preparation showed up tonight in how he played.

He had a little ankle injury. I don't know how severe it is. He tried to give it a go. We'll see. I'll probably have more information for y'all Monday. Unfortunately, it happened really, really early.

He's a really good football player. I tell Buster all the time, "Don't know what to do? Just hand it to 13. That will work, usually." He's phenomenal. He's a great kid and every bit as good as I thought he would be. I told him the night before the game, "Hey, I'm glad you're still here. Thanks for staying."

I'm very, very glad he's a Florida Gator. I love his playing style and demeanor. I also had a great appreciation for seeing his enthusiasm late in the game when he wasn't playing.

He was excited for his teammates to have opportunities and success when he saw Duke, Byron and some of the other guys in the room get carries. Rubio got in there. Seeing his excitement for his teammates says a lot about him, too.

Early on, we couldn't keep pace with them. Our defense was atrocious at times, quite honestly. We had a hard time keeping pace with them. I'll watch the tape, but I'm a little bit frustrated with how we played defensively at times.

I don't think we're as good as we think we are. I think we've got some guys who feel like we've arrived in some spots, and that will be addressed. We've got a lot of room to grow on defense.

If it doesn't happen really fast, we're going to get embarrassed and exposed pretty handily in some spots because that wasn't a great performance by us.

Hats off to FAU. They do some really good things. I love their quarterback. I played against the kid last year. I love the way he plays. He's tough, competitive and a leader. He's just a really good football player.

Zach does a great job offensively. Their offensive staff is really good at what it does, and they stress you out. That number eight, the little slot receiver, hit us on a slot fade. He's a good player. He averaged 12 targets a game last year for them. I'm sure he probably had about that tonight. I don't know how many he caught, but it felt like every time they threw to him, something good happened for them.

It was a good test. It was a really good test for a Week 1 game. They're a talented team, and I wish them nothing but the best.

It was a long day, but it was a great day. It was fun. A lot of fun. I tried to take in as much of it as I could, but at the end of the day, it's about winning a game. You're focused on what we've got to do to position ourselves to be successful on the field.

But all the great things around our program make this place what it is. The Gator Walk was unbelievable. When we left the hotel, there was a crowd of people in the hotel parking lot. I'm like, "All right, this is kind of cool. These people are waiting to see our guys walk to the bus at the hotel."

The support we have here is unbelievable, and I could not be more grateful for it. We're doing everything we can to make them proud. I'm very grateful for what Florida Gator Nation is all about.

It was fun. It was good. There was a lot of good in there and plenty of things to get better at. But I want our guys to have fun playing. I tell our team all the time that when you were growing up as a kid, you never said, "I want to go work football today." You always said, "I want to go play football." That doesn't mean it doesn't take hard work, but the work should be fun. Competing is fun, and making plays is fun.

The thing I'm most proud of tonight offensively is our perimeter blocking. Our receivers blocked their asses off. In the run game we created tonight, there were times on the perimeter when our receivers were competing to make blocks.

That says a lot about who they are. The character of a football player sometimes isn't revealed when he is getting opportunities for production. It's revealed by what he is doing to serve his team. I thought those guys blocked with edge and competitiveness.

That makes it fun. Competing is fun. I think it was a fun brand to watch tonight. We need to keep it up.

It was exhilarating. I was like, "All right, this is real." The energy in the stadium was — man, it was on fire. You could feel it. It was probably even better than I thought it was going to be. It was just really, really cool.

D.J. is one of those guys who is just really consistent. He's a high-level communicator. He has a high football IQ. He's smart, tough and dependable. I'm not surprised.

He showed it in the spring game. He had a pick on the glance route, and everybody was like, "Oh, the quarterback threw a pick." I'm like, "Well, that was a freaking unbelievable play that 33 made."

He's a really good player, and I'm glad he's on our football team. He has been a great pickup for us. He practices really hard every day. He invests a lot in his craft. He's just a steady, steady player. I'm not surprised by how he played because that's how he practices.

He had a big night. That was his first touchdown. I was getting on him all offseason. I'm like, "You haven't scored here. Everybody thinks you're this big-time player. We've got to see you score touchdowns."

To see him make the plays he made tonight — he had a couple of big plays. The first one was explosive. It was a great, great play by him. He's another unbelievable worker, so I'm not surprised. He competes his tail off and prepares the right way.

I'm happy for his success because he's one of the best leaders for a young player I've ever been around. He's a second-year player, a true sophomore, and he's a phenomenal leader and a great teammate.

That was good. He stuck his foot in the ground at the end of that run to get more and didn't just think the journey was over. I think he has taken on that challenge. We've challenged him with that sometimes on long, explosive runs.

I tell the receivers and the guys on the perimeter that an eight-, 10- or 12-yard run becomes a 40- or 50-yard run because they block better. They get on the safeties, and you're kind of nagging the defensive backs and getting in their way to create longer runs.

It was great to see him pop that long one. I'm proud of his performance.

Like I said, I thought our perimeter blocking was good. I thought certain guys on defense, at times, showed their contact courage. Maybe we weren't where we needed to be across the board, but I felt some physicality.

Procedurally, I'm probably most pleased with the offense. A lot of times in Game 1, there are delay-of-game penalties, illegal formations, false starts or a lot of other issues. It felt fairly clean in how we operated offensively.

Our special teams played really well. Durk hit the 50-plus-yarder. I think it was a 53-yarder. I thought he kicked the ball off well.

Other than the kickoff coverage where we missed a hit and didn't make the tackle, which I wasn't pleased with, I thought there were a lot of good areas.

At that point, I'm never going to be the one who tries to run up the score, per se. But I'm also not going to be someone who just shuts it down. Micah Jones scored the last touchdown, right? That was Micah, correct?

He is on the scout team all week right now. He's a young player who needs to improve for his own development and for our football team to continue growing. Byron Louis is kind of the fourth or fifth back right now, so I wanted to see him play.

I wanted to see Tramell operate and compete. I wanted to get Will Griffin in. If we had another drive, Will Griffin was probably going to go in. Those guys practice really hard.

At that point, I'm not saying, "Hey, we have to score again." If we score again, that's the nature of the deal. They were also bringing a lot of pressure. We had to get the ball on the perimeter and do some things because they were loading the box to stop the run late.

Those guys work incredibly hard all week. When their opportunities present themselves, we're going to let them play because we still have to develop those young players so they're more ready.

It was 1-0. That was the goal this week. We'll celebrate this a little bit tonight and then wake up tomorrow. We'll watch the tape, make corrections and then turn the page tomorrow night at about 5. Our staff meeting is at 4 tomorrow. As soon as that staff meeting is over, we'll watch special teams as a staff.

Then it's 1-0 and on to Campbell. It's about trying to win one game next week and focusing on that game all week. It's a good start. Being 1-0 was the goal this week, and we got there. Tomorrow at about 5, my mind will be 0-0 again.

It's just going into every game and focusing on one game at a time. It's coach speak, but that's how we operate.

Going back to it, we still need to figure out who we can rely on and who will be dependable. With the depth of our team, maybe on the line, there is still some room to figure that out. I wanted to see the backs go.

Rod Kearney came in. Caden (Jones) got in there, and Caden has started games before. He came in, and we need him to elevate his play. All those guys have to continue elevating. At offensive line, you have to get players ready to play because it's a long year.

You never know when their opportunity is going to come. You can't just think it doesn't matter whether he's getting better. We've got to get everybody in this program better. Everybody. Jadan Baugh has to get better. Everybody on our team has to continue getting better.

Those young linemen, Rod and Dice — Dice played some tackle that I liked. Those guys have to continue elevating so they can be dependable and reliable when their numbers are called.

Evan was available, but he had a little bit of a hip issue that wasn't feeling great. He didn't feel like he could do it. He was cleared to go but just didn't feel like he could push through it. I thought Duke did a really good job. London Montgomery is a good player back there, too. Byron Lewis did some good things tonight as well.

Follow us @GatorsWire on X, formerly known as Twitter, as well as Bluesky, and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Florida Gators news, notes and opinions.

title: Title-chasing Nottinghamshire lose Kyle Verreynne ahead of crucial County Championship run-in
description: Nottinghamshire's aspirations for the County Championship have taken a blow with the unexpected exit of Kyle Verreynne, who has been summoned by Cricket South Africa for an upcoming Test series. His absence during the final three crucial league fixtures could be detrimental as Nottinghamshire, currently in second place, scrambles to find a suitable replacement wicketkeeper for the rest of the season.
fullText:
Nottinghamshire's County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Cricket South Africa, ruling him out of the club's final three matches of the season.

Verreynne, 29, is in his third stint with Nottinghamshire and had initially agreed to play in all of the club's red-ball fixtures this summer. However, his central contract commitments with South Africa take priority as the Proteas prepare for a three-Test home series against Australia.

His final appearance for Nottinghamshire this season will come against Leicestershire at Trent Bridge, before he returns to South Africa.

Verreynne's departure comes at a crucial stage of Nottinghamshire's campaign. They currently sit second in the County Championship, four points behind leaders Somerset and one point ahead of third-placed Warwickshire, with just three rounds remaining.

The club will now have to manage the final stretch of the title race without their first-choice wicketkeeper, with fixtures against Hampshire, Sussex and Yorkshire still to come.

Despite his early departure, Verreynne said he would continue to follow Nottinghamshire's title challenge closely.

"I think I've said it so many times, the club's got a really special place. It's got a special place to me, so I'll be watching closely."

He added:

"The team's in a good position at the moment, playing some really good cricket. I think it's going to be quite an exciting run-in, so I'll be keeping a close eye."

Nottinghamshire Director of Cricket Mick Newell admitted that losing Verreynne at this point of the season was far from ideal, although the club understood South Africa's position.

"It's not ideal that we're losing Kyle at this point in the season, but we understand the decision made by Cricket South Africa, and he returns with our best wishes for a busy winter."

Newell also praised Verreynne's contribution during his latest spell with the club, saying his performances had helped Nottinghamshire put themselves in a strong position heading into the final weeks of the Championship.

"We've been very happy to have Kyle with us for most of the summer, during which his contributions have put us in a strong position as we head towards the final few matches," he said.

With several South African players being recalled from county cricket ahead of the Australia series, Nottinghamshire will now look for a replacement for Verreynne.

"There's always a lot of hard work being done behind the scenes to make sure we're prepared for every outcome, and we hope to confirm a replacement for Kyle as soon as we're able to," Newell added.

fullText:
The Washington State Cougars are getting ready to kickoff their 2026 football season and the Kirby Moore era with a week 1 rivalry game against the Washington Huskies.

WSU opens with their third new head coach in three years, with Moore arriving at WSU after being the offensive coordinator at Missouri. The Cougs will also be led by transfer quarterback Caden Pinnick.

The last time these two rivals squared off in Seattle, the Cougars emerged victorious 24-19 after a goalline stand to seal the game.

Kickoff is set for 1pm at Husky Stadium and will be broadcasted nationally on NBC and Peacock.

title: Alonso makes Caicedo confession after Chelsea beaten in midfield battle again
description: Xabi Alonso has admitted that Chelsea may have been too eager to get Moises Caicedo back into the team last week.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred so...
fullText:
Xabi Alonso has admitted that Chelsea may have been too eager to get Moises Caicedo back into the team last week.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Chelsea have just been beaten 2-1 by Arsenal, a disappointing result given the Blues took the lead.

There was a lot to like in the game, but Xabi Alonso's team just couldn't get control of the match in midfield. Arsenal's goals saw his team cut through far too easily.

If there was one player who could have made a difference it was Moises Caicedo. The midfielder has been out injured for a while, and his return as a sub last week ended in disaster when he was then subbed off just 11 minutes later, clearly in pain again.

Xabi Alonso (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Alonso doesn't want to give anything away about how bad the Ecuador star's issues are, but fans are desperate to know whether they can count on him coming back.

Alonso was coy once again in his post match press conference today:

"No, not longer term [injury], but it's about assessing the risk," the new Chelsea manager said.

"Probably last week we took him too early and I don't want to make the same mistake again."

With Caicedo fit, Chelsea have plenty of options to line up alongside him. While he's out injured, we look really lacking in bite in the middle.

Chelsea needed midfield control off the bench today and the best they could muster was Malo Gusto. This could be the start of a bigger problem for the Blues.

title: Champions Manchester City start with victory over newly-promoted Birmingham City
description: Manchester City got their Barclays Women’s Super League title defence off to a winning start with a 3-1 victory over newly-promoted Birmingham City at The Joie Stadium this afternoon.Khadija Shaw ne...
fullText:
Khadija Shaw netted a brace while Mary Fowler was also on target as The Cityzens were victorious on opening day.

It was the visitors who almost got off to a dream start. They won a corner inside the opening 30 seconds, but Marie Levasseur saw her effort cleared off the goal-line.

Océane Hurtré then almost capitalised on a back-pass, but home keeper Ayaka Yamashita did just about enough to deal with the danger.

At the other end, Shaw met Lauren Hemp's cross, but she couldn't beat Sophie Baggaley. Hemp soon produced another cross from the left which was met by Shaw, but she was again unable to take advantage,

Manchester City captain Alex Greenwood and Aoba Fujino had further efforts on the Birmingham City goal, but Baggaley was able to produce saves on both occasions. Fowler then slipped the ball to Shaw, who looked certain to score, but Neve Herron defended well and managed to perform a block.

Four minutes after half-time, Fowler broke the deadlock for the champions. The ball fell into the path of the Australian international and she slammed her shot into the bottom corner.

Shaw then finally got her goal. Kerstin Casparij swung the ball in after taking the corner and Shaw headed home.

Beth Mead almost had the dream start on her Manchester City debut. She attempted a shot at goal, but Baggaley once again was alert and stopped the ball. Hemp then cut the ball back into the path of Greenwood, but she ended up sending her strike over the crossbar.

Shaw scored her second goal and Manchester City's third in the final few moments of the game, it was not dissimilar from her first. Mead sent the ball in from a corner and once again, Shaw headed the ball into the net.

Birmingham City did manage to get a goal back in stoppage time through Hurtré. Jade Rose was caught in possession as Hurtré stole the ball and slotted it into the net.

Both sides are back in action next Sunday. Manchester City travel to Aston Villa while Birmingham City play host to Brighton & Hove Albion.

title: Stripped? Valentina Shevchenko’s coach explains what happened to her women’s flyweight title
description: After weeks of delays and behind-the-scenes attempts to cobble something meaningful together, UFC 332 in Salt Lake City, Utah finally has a championship main event: Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong for the vacant women’s flyweight belt. Wait, what? The flyweight belt that Valentina Shevchenko has defended a whopping nine times since 2018 across two title […]
fullText:
After weeks of delays and behind-the-scenes attempts to cobble something meaningful together, UFC 332 in Salt Lake City, Utah finally has a championship main event: Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong for the vacant women's flyweight belt.

Wait, what? The flyweight belt that Valentina Shevchenko has defended a whopping nine times since 2018 across two title runs? That's now vacant? When announcing Silva vs. Cong, they cited a "Bullet" injury but didn't really get into details on how the belt was put back up for grabs. A statement from Shevchenko's coach Pavel Fedotov gave a bit more info.

"We were supposed to fight on October 3 against Natalia Silva, but due to an injury to the ligaments in the shoulder and back, we decided not to push things and postpone the fight," Fedotov wrote (via Ushatayka). "Given that the recovery will take a long time, we've made the decision to temporarily vacate the belt, and once she recovers, she will fight for it again."

🏆 Two-time Flyweight champion
👏 Nine successful title defences 
💎 The FIRST and ONLY fighter to have eight rubies on their championship belt
🔥 Most consecutive single title defenses by a woman in UFC history (7)
💥 Tied with Amanda Nundes for most title fight wins in UFC… pic.twitter.com/VJ4NXSa99J

According to Fedotov, they're expecting the injury to take eight months to recover from.

In the past, you might expect to see an interim title go up for grabs after similar injuries taking under a year to heal. But these days, the UFC has gotten into the habit of asking its injured champions to relinquish their belts. Jamahal Hill did it when he ruptured his Achilles tendon, and so did Jiri Prochazka when he injured his shoulder. Now we've got Valentina Shevchenko doing it.

Hopefully these fighters are getting compensated well for giving up their hard earned championship gold so the UFC can patch holes in their matchmaking schedule with undisputed title fights. Hill and Prochazka never won back their belts after relinquishing. Will Shevchenko suffer the same fate?

fullText:

description: PlayStation Vita emulator. Contribute to cretz/vitaslop development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
A PlayStation Vita emulator that runs in a browser tab, and as a desktop app.

Everything happens on your own machine. There is no server, no Sony firmware, and
nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Early days. Some commercial games boot and play. Many do not. Homebrew works.
See the FAQ before expecting much.

https://cretz.github.io/vitaslop/

Your browser needs WebGPU, JSPI, shared memory, and OPFS. In practice that means a
recent Chrome or Edge on desktop or Android. The page checks all of it on load and
tells you what is missing. Firefox and Safari are not there yet.

Games you add are stored in the browser and stay there.

Download a build from Releases for
Windows, macOS, or Linux. Nothing to install. The desktop app also has a serve
command that hosts the same web version from your own machine.

vitaslop only works with games you own, from your own console, or with homebrew.
It provides no games and downloads nothing. Pirated games are not supported. The
"Add games" screen lists what it accepts.

Yes, 100%. vitaslop is an AI built and maintained project, and the code quality
reflects that. It is also why the usual expectations of a maintained repo do not
apply here.

No. This is an AI project, and the agent maintaining it writes all of the code.

Yes, and they get read. There is no promise that any of them get fixed. Reports
about one specific game are the least likely to, because most of them need that
game to investigate.

There is no compatibility list and there will not be one. Keeping it accurate is
more work than the project itself, and it turns into a promise.
Games tried is the handful the agent has played: playable, still
buggy, a record of what was done rather than a claim about what works.

Often it is not. Flagship Android phones on Chrome run plenty of this at full
speed. Demanding scenes are where it gives out, because a phone does the same work
as a desktop with roughly a third of the CPU, and full speed in those is not
always reachable.

No. There is no server side to this project at all. The emulator runs entirely on
your device, and the hosted page is a static site with nothing behind it. Games,
saves, and settings never leave your browser or your disk, and once the page has
loaded it makes no network requests.

Most of this had to be built from scratch, and some of it was more interesting
than expected.

Not a compatibility list. Owned games the agent has played, all US releases, all
playable and all still buggy. Anything not listed was never tried.

Rust and Node are the only requirements.

title: D2 Is Non-Profit
description: D2 is becoming an independent, donation-funded open-source project fiscally sponsored by Hack Club.
fullText:
Hello, I'm happy to share the news that D2 is now fiscally sponsored by
Hack Club!

The project was born and thus far developed as an open-core arm of a for-profit
company. The development of open-source D2 was funded by the closed-source IDE
(D2 Studio) and proprietary layout algorithm (TALA). The company is shutting down,
and D2 will continue as an independent, completely open-source, non-profit project
through Hack Club.

I will continue to maintain and improve D2. But my time commitment will be limited.
It's not my primary focus anymore, but I remain committed to its continued
development and am excited for the roadmap ahead.
If you have interest in becoming a maintainer, please email me at
alex@d2lang.com. High-quality maintenance and contributions
may be invited to enter into a paid contributor contract, funded by donations to
the non-profit. This would be ideal for a driven early-careerist with open-source
experience.

D2 thus far has been a product of handcrafted code. That era is over. This next
phase of D2 will be driven by AI. By this, I mean that all of my contributions will
use AI. I welcome AI contributions and will use AI to review your AI, etc. The
exception is writing -- I will author all blog posts and comms without AI.

In this manner, D2 will evolve at a rate that is orders of magnitude faster than
it has. Models will find ways to squeeze every millisecond of performance in a way
I could not. It'll make into reality the features that were daydreams pre-AI
because of limited engineering bandwidth, e.g. an isometric renderer, transpilers
from other diagramming languages, etc.

If you've invested a tiny part of your stack into D2, I hope this is received with
optimism more than concern. I wrote code ~every day for 10+ years, and have not
written any in the past year even though I'm working with software every day.
I know where the limitations are and have no intention of the project devolving
into slop.

I of course know this is somewhat controversial and has
downsides, and I'm not
recommending anything to anyone; I just wanted to be transparent about my plans to
the community and those who rely on D2.

I want to avoid bloat. To be clear, just because AI will allow me to make a Swiss
Army knife of a diagramming tool, I'd much rather spend the tokens on depth and
quality of a small, curated feature set. I'll want to add some plugin/module
system to easily add on things that don't belong in D2 core. For example, I still
plan for D2 to focus on the software architecture diagram use case and won't be
adding e.g. Venn diagrams, even if it'd be trivial to do so.

I still don't see a place for LLMs integrated into diagramming tools. I think
models are smart enough to just look at some examples and then take your specs or
code or whatever you want and turn it into a .d2 file. There doesn't need to be
yet another thinly tuned LLM interface for D2 to provide.

Since D2 is non-profit, we won't be supporting things that need servers. No MCP,
no API, no user accounts, no server rendering, no multiplayer. D2 Studio will be purely
client-side, usable completely offline.

That's all for now. I'll be making posts as TALA and D2 Studio are released.

Thank you to everyone who has engaged with us over the years, and especially
those who paid for the closed-source parts of it to fund its development. I'm
glad D2 has resonated with so many people and I still stumble upon it in blogs
and projects and mentions on the public internet and internal company channels.
It's always a leap of faith to adopt some new language with unknown motives and
continuity. I'm really happy about this direction for D2 and that the value of
this excellent IDE and layout algorithm can be shared with more people. I'm
excited for what's next.

If you'd like to donate to D2, please see this page
on how to do so and what the fund is used for.

title: Governing Well in the Algorithmic Age: The Foundations of Digital Statecraft
description: The digital substrate - data, algorithms, infrastructure, platforms, applications - is being governed without adequate conceptual foundations. The ability and legitimacy required to govern this substrate, and to govern with it, are simultaneously misaligned, contested, and structurally absent. We introduce digital statecraft as the organising concept for this emerging field, arguing that 'digital' reconstitutes the statecraft question rather than merely extending its domain. The concept operates on two dimensions - statecraft over digital systems, concerning the authority and capacity of the state in relation to the digital substrate itself, and statecraft with digital systems, concerning the deployment of algorithmic tools as instruments of governing authority. And it rests on two foundational requirements, technical coherence and legitimate authority, that are genuinely in tension.

description: Fast, scriptable CLI for the App Store Connect API. Automate TestFlight, builds, submissions, signing, analytics, screenshots, subscriptions, and more - rorkai/App-Store-Connect-CLI
fullText:
A fast, lightweight, and scriptable CLI for the App Store Connect API.
Automate iOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS release workflows from your terminal, IDE, or CI/CD pipeline.

Agent Skills for automating asc workflows including builds, TestFlight, metadata sync, submissions, and signing:
https://github.com/rorkai/app-store-connect-cli-skills

Install them globally so they are available across projects:

asc install-skills checks out reviewed commit
e30039abddbe388179324d0f9cdccb66c3843115 and copies its 23 skills directly
into the standard global agent-skills directory. It verifies the complete pack
and every installed file before succeeding, preserves unrelated skills and
unrelated lock entries, and pins the 23 ASC lock entries to the same reviewed
commit so external checks cannot update them from a mutable branch. It rolls
back the pack if any replacement fails. Only
git is required; the command does not execute Node.js, npx, an npm package,
or repository scripts.

If you want to confirm the binary works before configuring authentication:

The WinGet package is tracked in
GitHub Discussion #1552.
Until it appears in winget search asc, Windows users can download the signed
release binaries directly from the
GitHub releases page.

For source builds and contributor setup, see CONTRIBUTING.md.
Released binaries are self-contained and do not require a Go installation;
source builds use the toolchain version declared by go.mod.

Individual API keys have no issuer ID. Omit --issuer-id and pass --key-type individual:

Generate API keys at:
https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/access/integrations/api

If you are running in CI, a headless shell, or a machine where keychain access is not available, use config-backed auth instead:

asc chooses a default --output based on where stdout is connected:

You can still set a global preference:

asc uses visible lifecycle labels so you can judge support expectations before
depending on a command in CI or scripts:

asc sends pseudonymous command-level usage telemetry by default to help
maintainers understand which commands are used and where reliability work is
needed. Local events include a random installation ID, which lets events from
one installation be grouped over time; it is not derived from an Apple account
or machine identifier.

Telemetry includes the CLI version, operating system and architecture,
registered command path, duration, runtime context, invocation source, a
bounded outcome class, and the HTTP status when an API request fails. It may
include a sanitized public flag name. It does not include raw arguments,
stderr, error messages, flag values, response bodies, credentials, private
keys, Apple account, team, or issuer IDs, app or bundle IDs, usernames,
hostnames, repository names, or file paths.

Review or change telemetry at any time:

ASC_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 also disable telemetry. See the
telemetry reference for the exact event payload,
runtime handling, collector endpoint, and all controls.

Want to add yours?
asc apps wall submit --app "1234567890" --confirm

The command uses your authenticated gh session to fork the repo and open a pull request that updates docs/wall-of-apps.json.
It resolves the public App Store name, URL, and icon from the app ID automatically. For manual entries that are not on the public App Store yet, use --link with --name.
Use asc apps wall submit --dry-run to preview the fork, branch, and PR plan before creating anything.

For macOS TestFlight distribution, upload the exported .pkg first, then add
the processed build to a beta group:

--app is the App Store Connect app ID. If you use local Xcode build flags such
as --archive-path, also pass exactly one of --workspace or --project plus
--scheme; otherwise use a pre-exported .ipa or .pkg upload. Add
--submit --confirm to asc builds add-groups when distributing to an external
TestFlight group that needs beta app review submission.

Lower-level submission lifecycle commands (for debugging or partial workflows):

Readiness validation also warns when localized app names, subtitles,
descriptions, keywords, promotional text, or What's New copy still contains an
unmistakable template marker such as Lorem ipsum, TODO, TBD, or FIXME.
Lorem ipsum matches in any letter case. TODO, TBD, and FIXME match only
in uppercase because their lowercase spellings can be ordinary product wording.
The warning includes the locale, field, matched text, resource ID, and a
remediation step. It is advisory by default and becomes blocking only with
--strict:

Add the experimental --deep mode when a release needs checks that Apple
exposes only through its signed-in web app:

Deep validation reuses the file-backed cache without opening a login, Keychain,
password, or 2FA prompt. It checks App Privacy publication, relevant agreements,
and the first auto-renewable subscription attachment; availability and required
App Review fields still come from the public API. Paid-agreement relevance also
uses the app's current public price so an upfront-paid app isn't mistaken for a
free one. The private Apple endpoints can change without notice, so an
unavailable or changed response is unverified, not a false blocker. Add
--strict if CI must fail when a requested deep check can't be verified.

This lint intentionally does not judge platform names, roadmap language, or
beta/demo wording because those phrases can be legitimate product copy and
cannot be classified reliably offline. It also leaves shorter Lorem Ipsum
product wording and ordinary localized TODO copy without marker punctuation
unflagged; only template-like residue is reported.

Use asc metadata keywords audit before sync or apply when you want an ASO-focused
review of live keyword metadata across locales. It reports duplicate phrases, repeated
terms across locales, overlap with localized app name or subtitle, byte-budget usage,
and optional blocked terms from repeated --blocked-term flags or a text file.

Uploading screenshots for a single locale:

VERSION_LOCALIZATION_ID is the App Store version localization resource ID
from data[].id, not the locale code from attributes.locale.

For local capture coverage across multiple devices, locales, appearances, and
content fixtures, use an experimental matrix plan. Targets must already be
booted simulators; the command writes raw artifacts and an offline review
report, without uploading to App Store Connect:

See docs/design/screenshots-matrix.md for
the JSONC schema, isolated output layout, retry behavior, and review contract.

signing fetch downloads public certificates and provisioning profiles. A
usable signing identity also needs the matching private key; signing sync
can verify that local identity and share it through an encrypted Git
repository. For multi-target release testing, signing reconcile plans exact
device/profile changes. signing run provides a temporary macOS keychain only
for single-target archives. Multi-target exports must import the identity into
a job-scoped keychain and install every reconciled profile for the job-exclusive
macOS user. See the
signing guide for setup, CI, rotation, security
boundaries, and troubleshooting.

See docs/WORKFLOWS.md for local compile validation with
asc xcode build and a copyable .asc/deployment.json, .asc/workflow.json,
and ExportOptions.plist that use asc builds next-build-number,
asc xcode inject, asc xcode archive, asc xcode export --timeout 10m, and
asc publish testflight --group ... --wait.
Add --submit --confirm when
distributing to an external TestFlight group that needs beta app review submission.

The experimental asc xcode test command provides local unit/UI test execution
with structured results and preserved .xcresult bundles; see the same workflow
guide for an invocation.

Replace the example Xcode destination with a simulator installed on the host.

Apple Ads uses separate OAuth credentials from App Store Connect:

See guides/apple-ads-playbooks.mdx for
operator playbooks covering credential safety, org inspection, read-only smoke
tests, reporting, raw API usage, and guarded mutations.

Retention Messaging uses a dedicated In-App Purchase API key, separate from
App Store Connect API credentials:

See docs/architecture/storekit-retention-messaging.md
for the endpoint map, message and image requirements, environment variables,
and the full sandbox verification sequence.

Use built-in help as the source of truth:

For full command families, flags, and discovery patterns, see:

Local screenshot framing uses Koubou (pinned to 0.18.1) for deterministic device-frame rendering.
GitHub: https://github.com/bitomule/koubou

Simulator UI automation for screenshot capture and interactions uses AXe CLI.
GitHub: https://github.com/cameroncooke/AXe

The keyword difficulty methodology used by asc optimize keywords score is adapted from semihcihan's App Store Optimization CLI (MIT licensed).
GitHub: https://github.com/semihcihan/App-Store-Optimization-CLI

Contributions are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.

title: Germany's far-right AfD projected to win
description: ‌The far-right Alternative for Germany surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday but it was unclear whether it would be able to form a government on its own, according to exit polls after voting closed.
fullText:
‌The far-right Alternative for Germany surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday but it was unclear whether it would be able to form a government on its own, according to exit polls after voting closed.

The AfD won 44.5% of the vote, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives on 18.5%, with the center-left Social Democrats and environmental Greens both clearing the minimum threshold to enter parliament, an exit poll on the ARD broadcaster showed.

“We have made history in this country,” said Ulrich Siegmund, the 35-year-old AfD lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt, who drew thousands to his campaign rallies and who repeatedly cast victory in the state as a first step toward securing national power in federal elections due in 2029.

The result marks a major advance in the AfD’s push for national power and a significant setback for Merz’s coalition government, although it remained unclear whether the party would be able to form a state government. Turnout was around 76%, well above levels typically seen in state elections.

Much could depend on whether the left-wing populist BSW party, a potential AfD coalition partner, could also clear the threshold. Exit polls showed it just above or just below it.

State premier Sven Schulze congratulated the AfD and acknowledged the result showed it was the strongest party.

If the AfD is unable to rule outright, it could trigger a protracted process of coalition building by mainstream parties who are determined to keep out of power a party investigated for right-wing extremism by Germany’s domestic intelligence service.

The AfD’s program includes plans to push schools and cultural institutions toward more traditional values, curb immigration and overhaul public broadcasting.

While hard right parties have gained ground elsewhere in Europe, Germany’s Nazi past has contributed to a reluctance among mainstream parties to cooperate with the AfD, which wants a hard line on migration and warmer ties with Russia.

The AfD sees accusations of extremism as scaremongering and an insult to its millions of supporters.

Siegmund told CNN the election result will give his party the mandate to return to “sensible diplomacy” with both Russia and the United States.

“We need both if we as Germany want to be successful,” he said.

Alice Weidel, the party’s co-leader who called it an “historic” result, also told CNN: “We stood for election very clearly to represent the interests of our country — not Ukraine’s, not any other country’s.”

Sunday’s result is also another blow to the authority of Merz, whose popularity has sagged as his coalition government struggles to revive growth in Europe’s largest economy.

Describing Merz’ premiership as a “catastrophe,” Weidel labeled the AfD “a people’s party” that will seek to “deport everyone obligated to leave the country” and close the borders if given the mandate to govern at the federal level.

In a fracturing political landscape, the AfD is now Germany’s most popular party nationally, though other parties have ruled out forging coalitions with the AfD in a policy known as the “firewall.”

This story has been updated. CNN reporting from Sebastian Shukla contributed to this story.

title: HakoVM – Firecracker-class VMs in macOS, built by a macOS hacker
description: HakoVM: Firecracker-class microVMs for macOS, built for AI agents. One binary on Apple's Containerization framework. - las7/HakoVM
fullText:
Firecracker-class microVMs for macOS. Built for AI agents.

Install · For agents · vs Docker / Apple container / Lima · Design · Performance · Roadmap

Boot a hardware-isolated Linux VM from any OCI image in about 300 ms, run
commands in it at ~10 ms each, throw it away. No daemon, no Docker, no root.
The guest has no network card unless you give it one.

Full numbers and caveats in docs/comparison.md.

Firecracker needs KVM, so it does not run on a Mac. Docker Desktop, OrbStack
and Lima give you one big shared VM. Apple's container CLI is close, but it
is a general container tool with a daemon and a network stack you may not want.

HakoVM is a thin Swift runtime on Apple's open-source
Containerization framework, shaped
for one job: giving an AI agent a disposable machine it cannot escape from.

Code interpreter. Run model-generated code, get stdout, exit code and files back.
The guest cannot reach the network or any host path you did not mount.

Dependencies. The guest is offline by default. Install once with
--network and commit the result; every later run boots a copy-on-write
clone of it, offline, in about a second:

Commits layer (--from py-deps --commit py-deps-ml), and ten agents booting
from one commit each get their own clone. Mounting a host venv or
node_modules works too, and so does any image from a registry. See
docs/dependencies.md for when to use which.

Claude Code. Put every Bash call the agent makes inside a VM. Add to
.claude/settings.json:

The project directory is mounted at the same path, so the agent's relative and
absolute paths keep working. HAKO_IMAGE, HAKO_NETWORK=1 and HAKO_MOUNT
tune it. Round trip per command is about 0.7 s including the boot; a warm pool
is next on the roadmap to bring that to the exec latency.

MCP server. One command registers HakoVM as a tool for any MCP client:

The model gets hako_run (command, image or commit, timeout, cwd) and
hako_commits. Network and extra mounts are refused unless you start the
server with --allow-network / --allow-mounts.

Any language. hako run --json --timeout 60 -- ... prints one JSON
object with stdout, stderr, exit code and timings. See
docs/agents.md for all four integration paths and the
patterns that work.

Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or later. No sudo, no developer account.

That drops hako in ~/.local/bin and runs hako setup, which downloads a
28 MB Linux kernel built from Apple's Containerization config and caches
Apple's guest init plus alpine. Everything lives under ~/.hako.

hako is being built around six agent workloads: coding-agent shell, code
interpreter, parallel fan-out, browser agent, eval runs, and hosting untrusted
MCP servers. The design doc describes the primitives that
serve them: profiles, warm pools, host-terminated egress with hostname
allowlists, a credential broker, and commit/fork of prepared rootfs images.

See the roadmap for order and status.

title: PS5 Version of GTA 5 Now Playable on PC at Up to 60 FPS, via KytyPS5 Emulator
description: The KytyPS5 project can now run the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto 5 at up to 60 FPS on PC, a big jump from just a month ago when the game was still stuck at its splash screen. It looks like the emulator can only hold that performance for a few minutes before crashing, but that's still a massive...
fullText:
Sunday, September 6th 2026

 PS5 Version of GTA 5 Now Playable on PC at Up to 60 FPS, via KytyPS5 Emulator

 by DrUsmanSaleem

 Today, 11:53

 Discuss (1 Comment)

 The KytyPS5 project can now run the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto 5 at up to 60 FPS on PC, a big jump from just a month ago when the game was still stuck at its splash screen. It looks like the emulator can only hold that performance for a few minutes before crashing, but that's still a massive leap from where things stood back in July, when GTA 5 had only reached its in-game menus. A demo shared on X shows GTA 5 footage running on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D paired with a Radeon RX 7900 XT, with performance reportedly ranging from 40 to 60 FPS depending on the scene. The game is playable for a few minutes in the opening North Yankton scene, but crashes just before the police encounter.

Separately, at least four other PS5 titles have been shown hitting 60 FPS on the emulator, suggesting the progress isn't limited to one specific game. SharpEmu, the other major PS5 emulation project, is taking a slower approach, focusing on low-level accuracy and infrastructure first, before tackling individual game compatibility. All this is happening as PS5 hardware demand keeps climbing ahead of GTA 6's launch, with no PC version of Rockstar's next game confirmed yet. However, even if the emulation keeps advancing at this rate, it will be nearly impossible to get a playable build of GTA 6 on these emulators any time soon. Still, it's pretty cool to see PS5 emulation advancing so quickly.

description: Just drag and drop a folder, and all the local videos inside it are automatically cataloged into a database, turning them into your own offline video platform — with a familiar experience inspired by
fullText:
Localhub
 Just drag and drop a folder, and all the local videos inside it are automatically cataloged into a database, turning them into your own offline video platform — with a familiar experience inspired by YouTube, Netflix, and other popular video services.

No internet connection required. A completely **OFFline** video app. Add a directory, and all the local videos inside it are automatically cataloged into a database, turning the app into your own offline video platform — basically like having your own “famous Canadian video site” right on your computer. 😆

(It also supports YouTube- and Netflix-style layouts and experiences.)

It even supports separate virtual accounts and password protection, so the whole family can safely share the app!

https://youtu.be/Gz2Np25Z8jY

You can also leave comments on each video. For example, if there’s a scene you really like, just write down the timestamp — click it later, and you’ll jump straight to that moment. You can also write your thoughts and memories for each video, almost like adding notes to a family photo album.

Of course, it comes with all the features you’d expect from a modern video platform, including Theater Mode, live previews, and playlist creation.

But it also goes way beyond that, with features you won’t find on typical video sites: zooming into specific parts of a video, virtual-window playback, bullet-time jumps, and up to three simultaneous SRT subtitle tracks. You can even adjust subtitle timing if the subtitles are out of sync.

You could use it to keep a record of your pet’s growth, or create your own private, YouTube-like library containing only safe, family-friendly videos for your children.

In short, it’s like having your own private video platform — completely offline, customizable, and shared safely with your family.
